verdict.what_is_spun: UPL's India and international crop protection businesses, combined into a single listed pure-play crop protection platform
demerged_business_names: UPL Global Sustainable Agri Solutions Limited
verdict.reason: "Unlocking value for its shareholders by creation of an independent and focused crop protection platform"; two listed entities enable clearer value discovery, group simplification, independent capital raising and deleveraging
verdict.insiders: Promoters go 100% to 71.56% of UPL 2; UPL 2 Promoters (Shroff family, UPL Corp Mauritius, etc.) voluntarily locked for eighteen months from Listing Date; Mike Frank CEO of UPL Global
verdict.hidden_value: The spin holds the bulk of earnings: UPL Cayman turnover USD 4,187 Mn vs UPL 1's INR 53,313 Mn, demerged India undertaking 31.15% of turnover; "world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform", 140+ countries. Parent keeps diversified residual; scheme drives deleveraging
verdict.selling_pressure_why: 1 for every 1 entitlement puts UPL 2 shares with every UPL holder at a fresh listing; promoter lock-in leaves only 28.44% public float
verdict.listing_timeline: Press release dated February 20, 2026: "The transaction is expected to be completed within 12–15 months, subject to the timely receipt of regulatory and other required approvals"; BSE "no adverse observations" and NSE "No Objection" letters dated July 29, 2026; "Subsequently, UPL 2 will be listed on Indian stock exchanges pursuant to the Scheme"
verdict.read_next: Scheme/abridged prospectus for UPL 2: assets and liabilities transferred, debt allocation, and 3-year revenue, EBITDA, PAT
verdict.quote: Bringing our crop protection businesses under one platform creates the world's second largest listed pure-play crop protection platform.

verdict.what_is_spun: HEG's graphite business — graphite electrodes and other carbon products — demerged into HEG Graphite Limited
demerged_business_names: manufacturing graphite electrodes (including other carbon products)
verdict.reason: Core businesses (graphite electrodes; thermal and hydel power) acquired critical mass and need flexibility, independence, focused management; segregation to unlock value and attract different investors, lenders and strategic partners.
verdict.insiders: Promoter/Promoter Group holds 50,000 shares (100%) of HEG Graphite pre-Scheme, 56.28% post-Scheme on mirror basis; in HEG Limited promoter stake rises 56.28% to 60.72% via BEL amalgamation.
verdict.hidden_value: Registered Valuer puts the Graphite Business at Rs. 393.4 per share versus Rs. 124.0 for HEG post-demerger; HEG Graphite post-Scheme holds Rs. 4,329.30 cr assets, Rs. 3,810.32 cr net worth and all Rs. 1,309.63 cr revenue.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents do not discuss index treatment, shareholder size or listing mechanics; entitlement is 1:1 mirror of existing holders.
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated; the August 18, 2026 disclosure says only that 'The Scheme shall become effective upon receipt of the certified copy of the Order passed by the Hon'ble Tribunal and fiting of the same with the Registrar of Companies', with certified copies awaited
verdict.read_next: Valuation Report dated 10 March 2025 (Annexure J) behind the Rs. 393.4 per share Graphite Business value.
verdict.quote: unlocking the value of each of the businesses for the shareholders of the Demerged Company, attracting different sets of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders having a specific interest in the respective businesses and providing better flexibility in accessing capital;

verdict.what_is_spun: Bio Pharma undertaking and Spirits & Biofuel undertaking demerged from India Glycols into two new companies
verdict.reason: not stated — the NCLT order says the "rationale of the scheme" was discussed in the first motion order dated 15.01.2026, which is not in these documents
verdict.insiders: Not stated beyond voting: Promoter and Promoter Group cast 3,99,67,854 of 4,42,48,626 votes, 100% in favour; shares allotted pro rata to all holders, so promoter holding mirrors across both resulting companies. No incentive detail.
verdict.hidden_value: Cost-of-acquisition split prices Spirits & Biofuel highest at 47.62%, Bio Pharma 20.61%, residual India Glycols 31.77%. Parent carries roughly INR1,100 crore term loan at 31 March 2026, with INR467 crore for prepayment; rating on watch list until demerger completes.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Two new entities handed to every holder (1-for-3 EBL, 1-for-1 IGSL); no index membership or trading history stated.
verdict.listing_timeline: Said 21st August, 2026: shares allotted on Record Date 2nd September, 2026 "shall, in terms of the Scheme, be listed on the bourses of the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and the BSE Limited subject to the applicable regulations and the necessary regulatory approvals" — no listing date given; allotment was intimated 8th September, 2026 and the Scheme became effective 1st September, 2026
verdict.read_next: First motion NCLT order dated 15.01.2026 for the scheme rationale, plus the per-unit debt profile promised on the call
verdict.quote: The Scheme became effective from 1st September, 2026.

verdict.what_is_spun: Clinical Services undertaking of NHIC — 10 Bengaluru clinics — demerged into listed parent NHL
verdict.reason: Clinics had developed dependencies on hospital infrastructure and duplicated admin functions; separation lets NHIC pursue the Aarogyam preventive healthcare business exclusively while NHL integrates clinics for unified patient pathways and cost savings.
verdict.insiders: Not stated. No change in shareholding pattern; NHIC remains a 100% wholly owned subsidiary of NHL, with no cash consideration and no shares issued.
verdict.hidden_value: Clinical Services is tiny — Rs 39.94 crore, 1.11% of NHL standalone FY25 turnover — and was a cost-duplicating dependency; the retained asset-light Aarogyam preventive platform is where NHIC claims growth and 'demonstrated investor interest'.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No shares issued, no new listing, no index change; demerged business is 1.11% of turnover and stays inside listed NHL.
verdict.listing_timeline: Per the December 12, 2025 filing: 'The Resulting Entity is a listed entity. There is no requirement of any new listing of shares as there is no consideration involved in the Demerger in view of the Demerged Company being a wholly owned subsidiary of the Resulting Company.'
verdict.read_next: NHIC standalone financials — Clinical Services profitability; and the Meridian Medical Research & Hospital amalgamation scheme filed September 27, 2025.
verdict.quote: The Clinical Services undertaking of NHIC, comprising 10 clinics located in Bengaluru, shall be demerged to NHL.

verdict.what_is_spun: Vedanta's power generation assets into Talwandi Sabo Power Ltd ("Vedanta Power"), alongside aluminium, oil & gas, iron & steel demergers
demerged_business_names: merchant power business of Vedanta Limited
verdict.reason: To create focused, pure-play sector companies that unlock long-term value through sharper strategic focus, independent capital allocation and governance, simplifying Vedanta's structure and giving investors direct exposure to sector-leading assets.
verdict.insiders: Promoter/management stake in the new entity not stated; shareholders of Vedanta Limited receive shares in each of the four resulting listed entities in proportion to existing holdings, ensuring continuity of ownership.
verdict.hidden_value: Oil & gas entity MEL's net worth is projected to rise from negative INR 178 crores to positive INR 13,507 crores upon demerger, while that entity also absorbs large uncrystallised GoI claims (counterclaim of 8,596.80 crores).
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Four new sector-specific entities distributed pro-rata to all VEDL holders; index treatment and float size not stated in documents.
verdict.listing_timeline: Nov 2025 call: "This will set the stage for the listing of all five demerged entities by the end of FY '26"; Jan 2026 call: NCLT approved the scheme on 16 December 2025, certified copy received 21 January 2026, "targeting 1st of April"; power demerger approval still pending in a separate NCLT proceeding, and listing is subject to further regulatory and stock exchange approvals.
verdict.read_next: The separate NCLT proceeding on the merchant power demerger, plus TSPL's share-entitlement ratio and net-worth certificate in the Scheme.
verdict.quote: Shareholders of Vedanta Limited will receive equity shares in each of the four resulting listed entities (in addition to their shareholding in Vedanta Limited) in proportion to their existing holdings, ensuring continuity of ownership while enabling direct participation in the growth trajectories of individual businesses.

verdict.what_is_spun: GE Power India Limited's boiler manufacturing business, demerged into JSW Energy Limited
demerged_business_names: GE Power India Ltd.'s Boiler Manufacturing Business
verdict.reason: Acquisition of the boiler manufacturing business "significantly enhances our in-house capabilities" with technology; described as one of three strategic developments during the quarter.
verdict.insiders: not stated
verdict.hidden_value: Not stated; documents disclose only that the boiler manufacturing business moves into JSW Energy, adding in-house boiler technology and manufacturing capability. No financials, valuation or share-exchange terms given.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No share-exchange ratio, consideration, size or index treatment stated; JSW Energy is already listed and no new entity lists.
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated
verdict.read_next: The Scheme and explanatory statement on www.jswenergy.in — share exchange ratio and boiler business financials.
verdict.quote: We have entered into a Scheme of Arrangement with GE Power India Ltd. to acquire its boiler manufacturing business.

verdict.what_is_spun: The "Identified Business Undertaking" of Apollo Hospitals, demerged into Apollo Healthtech Limited, with Apollo Healthco and Keimed merged in
demerged_business_names: Apollo Healthco Limited ("Transferor Company 1", also the name Resultant Company will take)
verdict.reason: Calls cite enhancing "long-term shareholder value" and being "well positioned to capture the full benefits of scale with the combined entity to achieve a run rate of INR 25,000 crore"; scheme text's rationale not in excerpt.
verdict.insiders: Demerged Company holdings: Suneeta Reddy (MD) 29,37,066 shares (2.04%), Chairperson 10,43,915 (0.73%), Shobana Kamineni non-executive director. AHL Promoter becomes executive chairperson of Resultant Company; new ESOP scheme; Rasmeli upside-share agreement with Shobana Kamineni and identified employees.
verdict.hidden_value: Separation collects Healthco plus Keimed distribution into one listed vehicle targeting a ~INR 25,000 crore run rate, with promoter as executive chairperson, fresh ESOPs, and Rasmeli's upside-sharing — incentives loaded into the new entity, not the parent.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Resultant Company shares issued to all AHEL shareholders on Record Date 1 and newly listed; healthtech/distribution business distinct from hospitals.
verdict.listing_timeline: May 2026 call: "hopeful the demerger process is completed by Q4 FY27 as planned earlier" and "by Q4 FY27, end of December or early Q4 FY27 is when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed"; shareholder meeting June 24, 2026, then NCLT "some 3, 4 months to close".
verdict.read_next: Annexure 17 and 33-34: revenue and net-worth of the Identified Business Undertaking versus AHEL; then Annexure 31 valuation report.
verdict.quote: The Demerged Company has filed the Scheme with the Registrar of Companies on April 15, 2026 in form GNL-1.

verdict.what_is_spun: HUL's Ice Cream Business Undertaking, demerged into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited, a pure-play India ice cream company
verdict.reason: "Separation beneficial for both Companies" — tailoring the operating model for ice cream cold chain, and focusing investment algorithm and incentives to ice cream.
verdict.insiders: Promoter/management stake not stated. HUL holders get 1 KWIL share per HUL share. HUL CFO Ritesh Tiwari is non-executive director; Prashant Premrajka executive director & CFO, Chitrank Goel deputy MD.
verdict.hidden_value: A #2 India ice cream player with top-tier gross margins whose EBITDA collapsed from 7.1% (FY24-25) to 0.0% (H1 FY25-26) on cocoa, GST and standalone costs — with a margin-recovery roadmap in an 11%-growth market; parent gains 50-60bps margin.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: 1-for-1 shares to every HUL holder of a small, currently zero-EBITDA pure-play cold-chain ice cream company; different industry from FMCG parent.
verdict.listing_timeline: Oct 2025 call: "We expect to complete the demerger by December, with the listing anticipated in Quarter 4 of Financial Year 2026, subject to necessary regulatory approvals"; Feb 2026 call: "we have completed the demerger of the Ice Cream business this quarter".
verdict.read_next: KWIL's information memorandum filed with the Stock Exchanges, especially its "Risk Factors" and the Unilever brand/technology royalty agreement.
verdict.quote: We expect to complete the demerger by December, with the listing anticipated in Quarter 4 of Financial Year 2026, subject to necessary regulatory approvals

verdict.what_is_spun: The power transmission business undertaking of Triveni Engineering, vested into Triveni Power Transmission Limited
verdict.reason: Management: the amalgamation of SSEL and demerger of the Power Transmission business are "to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies"; strategic push towards the independent listing of TPTL.
verdict.insiders: Not stated as a stake or incentive. Every equity shareholder gets 1 TPTL share (face value INR 2) per 3 Triveni shares (INR 1), so holdings mirror the parent.
verdict.hidden_value: Separation exposes Power Transmission as a standalone with "its own dynamics": capex programmes "progressing very smoothly", continuing export market, more orders expected near-term. EBITDA-margin impact post-demerger was asked about but not quantified.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents state only the 1-for-3 ratio and small INR 2 face value; no size, index-exclusion or shareholder-base detail given.
verdict.listing_timeline: Not stated as a date. Jun 2026 call: "strategic push to clearly move towards, of course, the independent listing of TPTL"; demerger record date fixed as Wednesday, July 22, 2026 (filing dated July 11, 2026); scheme effective May 19, 2026, demerger appointed date April 1, 2026.
verdict.read_next: Annexure-21: TPTL abridged-prospectus information (SEBI ICDR Part E) at page 500 of the NCLT notice
verdict.quote: Consequent upon the Scheme becoming effective, the power transmission business undertaking of the Company stood transferred to and vested into TPTL with effect from the Dernerger Appointed Date i.e. April 1,2026.

verdict.what_is_spun: The Power Evacuation Business (substation / evacuation infrastructure) of Inox Green Energy Services Limited
demerged_business_names: formerly known as Resco Global Wind Services Private Limited
verdict.reason: Segregation of business verticals with separate risks, rewards and investors; consolidation of Power Evacuation Business into IRSL to unlock value; establish IGESL as a pure-play O&M player; two independently focused listed entities.
verdict.insiders: Not stated for promoter/management stake in IRSL; documents only state "no promoter shareholder of the Demerged Company is a non-resident" and Inox Green shareholders get 122 IRSL shares per 2,000.
verdict.hidden_value: Parent becomes pure-play O&M with depreciation eliminated on demerged asset blocks, so "our PBT would be equivalent to EBITDA"; only ~INR 10 crore revenue leaves. IRSL carries large losses, INR 96.80 crore tax demand and heavy secured/unsecured debt.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Tiny entitlement (122 shares per 2,000 held) creates small odd-lot positions in a differently-focused EPC/evacuation business newly listed on BSE and NSE.
verdict.listing_timeline: No listing date stated. Affidavit of 20.01.2026: the Resulting Company "shall continue to remain in existence after sanction of the Scheme and its shares shall be listed on the BSE and NSE"; NCLT order pronounced 13.03.2026, certified copy received 27th April 2026; Nov 2025 call referred to "subsequent listing of Inox Renewable solution as an EPC arm of Inox Wind".
verdict.read_next: Annexure-A Scheme clauses 8.1(b)/8.2(g) and IRSL's standalone financials behind the INR 96.80 crore AY 2023-24 demand.
verdict.quote: The effectiveness of the proposed Scheme will lead to two listed entities with one entity continuing with the O&M business and other entity carrging on the EPC and Power Evacuation business.

verdict.what_is_spun: The NBFC Business (retail mortgage lending: home loans and LAP) of Sammaan Finserve, transferred to listed parent Sammaan Capital
verdict.reason: RBI directed that no other group entity hold an NBFC-ICC/HFC licence; to comply, SFL's NBFC Business is consolidated into SCL, leaving SFL to enter insurance broking/insurtech.
verdict.insiders: No shares allotted as consideration (SFL is wholly owned). Directors' only material interest: Naveen Uppal holds 678 and Rajiv Gandhi 2,50,000 fully paid-up SCL shares.
verdict.hidden_value: Not a value-releasing spin: assets move up into the listed parent, widening SCL's capital and asset base. The stated residual is SFL's unlisted 'independent fintech structure' planning insurance broking/insurtech, retained by SCL.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: No equity consideration issued and no new listed entity; only a 1:1 NCD exchange from SFL to SCL.
verdict.listing_timeline: not stated
verdict.read_next: Valuation Report dated 31.12.2025 by Transaction Square Advisory (Annexure A-14) for the Demerged Undertaking's assets and liabilities.
verdict.quote: The Demerged Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Resulting Company.

verdict.what_is_spun: TCIL's resorts and resort management business — 6 resorts under the Nature Trails brand — into SHRL
demerged_business_names: Resorts and Resort Management Business of TCIL
resorts and resort management business of Demerged Company
verdict.reason: Unlock value for TCIL shareholders, attract differentiated investor cohorts, sharper strategic and operational focus per vertical; SHRL's hotel expertise suits the business and SHRL is poised to list separately.
verdict.insiders: Promoters hold 100% of SHRL pre-scheme, 65.55% post (including 7% held by TCIL); ESOP Trust 2.16% via 65,70,000 accelerated ESOP Options 2024. Fairbridge Capital (Mauritius)/Fairfax promotes TCIL with 63.83%.
verdict.hidden_value: The demerged undertaking is tiny — INR 70 Crores, ~0.4% of standalone turnover — yet SHRL, the receiving company, is "a leading leisure hospitality company with over 72 resorts, hotels and retreats across 62 locations" that will now be separately listed and valued.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Documents state 32.30% indicative public float in a hospitality entity spun from a travel company; nothing stated on index exclusion.
verdict.listing_timeline: No listing date given. Filing (March 20, 2026): "Yes, the Resulting Company is proposed to be listed on BSE and NSE pursuant to the Scheme upon receipt of requisite approvals from the Stock Exchanges"; consolidation "expected to be completed... within 15 to 18 months from the date of approval of the Scheme by the Board." May 2026 call, Debasis Nandy: "when we took the Board approval for this particular demerger project, we said that it will take us 12 to 15 months. The project is currently on track. We have applied to the NSE and the BSE for relevant approvals."
verdict.read_next: SHRL standalone financials and the Scheme's share entitlement ratio report behind 81-for-100.
verdict.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.

verdict.what_is_spun: The Mobility Undertaking — Refex's EV fleet mobility vertical serving B2B and B2B2C platforms
verdict.reason: "in line with our strategy to unlock focused value creation for all our stakeholders"; post-demerger mobility pursues its growth plan independently with strategic and financial flexibility, running its own debt
verdict.insiders: Mirror shareholding: RGML is a 100% subsidiary so no valuation was required and all shareholders get matching RML shares. Promoter stake or incentives in RML not stated.
verdict.hidden_value: No valuation was ever ascertained for the mobility vertical (management said none was required). RML takes its own debt; RIL carries Rs 158.90 cr secured and Rs 347.67 cr unsecured creditors as on March 31, 2026.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Mirror shareholding hands 92,973 RIL holders a small, newly listed EV-mobility entity in a different industry with no set valuation.
verdict.listing_timeline: No listing date stated. Jan 2026 call: "we currently are waiting for some final NOCs from the lenders. As soon as it comes, the scheme is ready to be filed and we are trying our best to ensure that this can happen as soon as possible." Nov 2025 call: asked "at what point do we see that company getting listed completely as a separate unit?" — no timeline given in reply. Process dates on file: BSE/NSE observation letters March 16, 2026; NCLT order June 18, 2026; shareholder and creditor meetings August 5, 2026, all approving.
verdict.read_next: The Composite Scheme annexed to the Notice dated July 03, 2026 — share entitlement ratio and debt split to RML
verdict.quote: Post-demerger, the mobility vertical will pursue its growth plan independently with strategic and financial flexibility.

verdict.what_is_spun: REL's financial services business — lending, broking, investment activities and ancillary and support services
verdict.reason: Separate financial services from insurance into two focused independent listed entities, enabling differentiated strategy, distinct investor sets, sharper management focus, tailored risk/compliance frameworks, and unlocking value for REL shareholders.
verdict.insiders: No change in REL's shareholding pattern; RFL's post-scheme pattern mirrors REL's 1:1, promoter stake carried over. Post-demerger each entity gets dedicated leadership, already hiring; rewards mapped to business outcomes.
verdict.hidden_value: Demerged financial services turnover was only INR 457.29 crore, 6.2% of REL's consolidated turnover — the parent keeps Care Health Insurance, i.e. the bulk. RFL is an unlisted RBI middle-layer NBFC entering public markets with mirror shareholding.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Small relative business (6.2% of turnover), mirror 1:1 distribution to all REL holders, NBFC in different sector from insurance parent.
verdict.listing_timeline: Press release dated February 14, 2026: "The company endeavours to complete the process and list RFL in Q1 of FY28"; NSE letter dated July 07, 2026 requires listing and trading to commence within sixty days of receipt of the NCLT order.
verdict.read_next: RFL's Information Memorandum / abridged prospectus disclosures — revenue, PAT, EBITDA and post-demerger balance sheet.
verdict.quote: Post-demerger, RFL will be listed on BSE and NSE with mirror image shareholding as REL.

verdict.what_is_spun: The Chemicals / Adhesive Business Undertaking of Astral Limited, vested into Astral Chemie Limited (paints & coatings subsidiary)
verdict.reason: Dedicated leadership and sector expertise, focused capital deployment, specialised board, shared R&D synergies with paints and coatings, and unlocking distinct equity value by eliminating the conglomerate discount.
verdict.insiders: Promoters hold 100% of Resulting Company pre-scheme, 54.22% post-scheme (indicative); mirror 1:1 shareholding, no cash consideration; a specialised Board for the Resulting Company. No incentive terms stated.
verdict.hidden_value: Chemicals turnover ₹12,663 million (21% of Astral's total) would combine with the paints and coatings business under one platform; documents claim conglomerate discount removal. The independent consultant found the Chemical Business lacked current scale.
verdict.selling_pressure_why: Scheme withdrawn July 29, 2026, so no shares were issued; chemicals was 21% of turnover and a different industry.
verdict.listing_timeline: "Upon the effectiveness of the Scheme and subject to receipt of regulatory approvals, the New Shares will be listed on the Stock Exchanges" (June 25, 2026); no date given, and on July 29, 2026 the Board withdrew the Scheme so no listing will occur.
verdict.read_next: Astral's future disclosures and segment financials on the Chemical Business reaching "scale and financial strength" for a revived demerger.
verdict.quote: Accordingly, the Board has decided to withdraw the Composite Scheme of Arrangement now, and no further steps will be undertaken in relation to the proposed the Composite Scheme of Arrangement.

verdict.rationale: Thomas Cook (India) Ltd. (TCIL) is carving out its Resorts and Resort Management Business and demerging it into Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd. (SHRL), its wholly owned hospitality subsidiary, which will then be listed separately on BSE and NSE. The Board's stated logic is a split by industry dynamics: TCIL is a travel company (Travel Services and Financial Services/foreign exchange) that happens to own and operate resorts across India — including curated segments like Adventure Holidays (trekking, kayaking, rafting, zip lining), Educational trips (survival skills, self-defence, nature appreciation) and Corporate Getaways (team building, wellness, leadership) — while SHRL already has deep experience running hotels for a different demographic, so TCIL and SHRL's Boards believe the resort assets 'would reap more benefits on account of expertise of SHRL in similar kind of business.' SHRL's Board separately says SHRL has 'matured over the years' and is 'well poised to chart its own growth path' as a standalone listed company in the fast-growing hospitality industry. The demerged undertaking is small in TCIL's revenue terms — INR 70 crore of turnover for the year ended 31 December 2025, about 0.4% of standalone turnover — so the move is about focus, structure and value rather than size: management (Mahesh Iyer) said the restructuring lets TCIL 'streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business,' and that the scheme will 'unlock value for our shareholders.' The demerger rides inside a composite scheme that also (a) merges three dormant, non-operative wholly owned subsidiaries — TC Visa Services (India), Jardin Travel Solutions and Borderless Travel Services — which are 'incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs,' and (b) consolidates TCIL's face value 4 Re-1 shares into 1 Rs-4 share, followed by a reduction of face value from Rs 4 to Rs 3 with no payment to shareholders; management said the face-value consolidation plus the dormant-subsidiary merger 'further simplifies our corporate structure and improves our Earnings Per Share.' The scheme says the consolidation should improve key financial ratios so the share price better reflects intrinsic value and conveys 'stronger financial stability and valuation metrics.' No cash changes hands: TCIL shareholders get 81 SHRL shares of Rs 10 each for every 100 TCIL shares of Re 1 each, leaving SHRL at an indicative 65.55% promoter (including 7% retained by TCIL), 2.16% ESOP trust and 32.30% public, with 65,70,000 ESOP 2024 options accelerated; TCIL's own shareholding pattern is unchanged. Timing context matters: FY26 consolidated income rose 3% to INR 83,982 million but EBT fell 14% to INR 3,268 million on the Middle East geopolitical crisis (hitting Desert Adventures, the Middle East destination management unit, and DEI, with ~50% of revenue from UAE), while TCIL sits on roughly INR 16 billion (INR 1,600 crore) of forex float against INR 277 crore debt, i.e. ~INR 730-740 crore net cash.
verdict.evolution: The idea first surfaced from the sell side, not management: on the May 2024 call Dhaval Desai asked whether Sterling's margin profile would hold and whether 'at any point in time in future, would we think of demerging Sterling and listing it separately' — Vikram Lalvani answered only the margin half (hospitality margins run 30-35%, Sterling is already there and should stay at 34-36%) and the passage shows no commitment on the demerger. Nothing further appears until March 2026, when the Board granted in-principle approval for the demerger of the resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts, announced as a 'strategic divestment.' By the May 2026 call it had become live execution: Mahesh Iyer framed it as capital-structure streamlining and value unlock, Vikram Lalvani confirmed 'the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated' alongside Sterling's own brand re-architecture over the next 2-4 quarters, and after Ananya Khanna (Alpha Alternatives) asked for timeline clarity, Debasis Nandy said the Board-approved 12-15 month plan is on track, applications are filed with NSE and BSE with queries being answered, and completion is still expected by Q1 FY28 — the original guided timeline.

points.point: An analyst, not management, raised the separation idea — asking whether Thomas Cook would ever demerge Sterling and list it separately; the passage shows no management answer to that part.
points.quote: And also, at any point in time in future, would we think of demerging Sterling and listing it separately?

points.point: Vikram Lalvani answered only the margin question, positioning Sterling as already at best-in-class hospitality margins (industry 30-35%, several brands still aspiring to 35%) and guiding 34-36% going forward — the profitability case that later underpins a standalone listing.
points.quote: Now even going forward, it will be in this range of 34% to 36%.

points.point: Mahesh Iyer disclosed that the Board granted in-principle approval in March 2026 for demerging the resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts, describing it as a strategic divestment that will unlock shareholder value.
points.quote: Before we move on to the segmental analysis, I will discuss the strategic divestment announcement that was made in March 2026, where the Board has granted in -principle approval for the demerger of our resort business into Sterling Holiday Resorts.

points.point: For TCIL specifically, the stated benefit is a cleaner capital structure and undivided resource focus on the two core engines — Travel and Financial Services.
points.quote: For Thomas Cook (India) Limited, this restructuring allows us to streamline our capital structure and concentrate our resources on our core Travel and Financial Services business.

points.point: Management bundled the demerger with a face-value consolidation and the absorption of three dormant subsidiaries, citing a simpler corporate structure and higher EPS as direct shareholder benefits.
points.quote: The consolidation of our face value per share, along with the merger of the three dormant subsidiaries , further simplifies our corporate structure and improves our Earnings Per Share, directly benefiting our shareholders.

points.point: Vikram Lalvani said Sterling has attained meaningful scale (Sterling ONE on distributed ledger technology, direct access to 7,000 travel partners and 360 corporates), is planning a full brand re-architecture over the next 2-4 quarters, and that the demerger from Thomas Cook has been initiated in parallel.
points.quote: In parallel, as you are aware, the demerger process from Thomas Cook has also been initiated.

points.point: Lalvani framed Sterling's post-transformation phase as accelerated value creation — faster and better growth with stronger operating leverage, cash generation and disciplined capital allocation — the standalone-entity pitch.
points.quote: Sterling is now just not growing faster: it is growing better with greater predictability, stronger operating leverag e, increasing cash generation and disciplined capital allocation.

points.point: An institutional investor, Ananya Khanna of Alpha Alternatives, pressed management for demerger timeline clarity alongside questions on the weak financial services segment and monsoon risk to resorts.
points.quote: And third thing, if we could get some clarity on the timeline for the demerger, that would be great.

points.point: Debasis Nandy confirmed the process is on track against the 12-15 month plan approved by the Board, with NSE and BSE applications filed and exchange queries being answered, and completion expected by Q1 FY28 per the original timeline.
points.quote: We expect this process to get completed by Q1 of FY '28, which was the original timeline that we had intimated.

points.point: Context for the restructuring: FY26 income rose 3% to INR 83,982 million but EBT fell 14% to INR 3,268 million on the Middle East war, which hit Desert Adventures and DEI (~50% of DEI revenue from UAE).
points.quote: On a full year basis, while our income increased to INR 83,982 million, a 3% increase on a consolidated basis, our EBT was impacted by the geopolitical crisis and was 14% lower than last year at INR 3,268 million.

points.point: Balance-sheet backdrop confirmed on the call: roughly INR 1,600 crore of forex float against INR 277 crore of debt, implying about INR 730-740 crore of net cash; float balances are flat versus December because customers are not travelling and money is sitting on cards.
points.quote: 1,600 crores of float minus the debt of INR 277 crores. So net cash with the company as of now should be closer to about INR 730 crores - INR740 crores.

points.point: The demerged undertaking is tiny relative to TCIL's standalone revenue base, sizing the transaction as a focus/structure move rather than a disposal of material revenue.
points.quote: The turnover of the Demerged Undertaking for the year ended 31st December 2025 was INR 70 Crores representing ~0.4% of the total standalone turnover of the Company for the year ended 31st December 2025.

points.point: The core operating argument is capability fit: TCIL's resorts and resort-management business (Adventure Holidays, Educational trips, Corporate Getaways) should sit with SHRL, which already runs hotels for a different demographic.
points.quote: TCIL and SHRL's Board believes that the Resorts and Resort Management Business of TCIL would reap more benefits on account of expertise of SHRL in similar kind of business.

points.point: SHRL's Board argues the subsidiary has matured enough to set its own strategy and be valued as a standalone hospitality listing.
points.quote: Further, SHRL's Board is of the view that SHRL matured over the years and is well poised to chart its own growth path and operate as a separate listed entity in the fast -growing hospitality industry.

points.point: The overarching objective is to segregate business verticals so each listed entity chases opportunities matched to its own industry dynamics, improving operational efficiency and profitability.
points.quote: In this manner, the two listed entities can each pursue growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics, leading to improved operational efficiencies and profitability.

points.point: Consideration is all-stock and no cash: 81 SHRL shares of Rs 10 face value for every 100 TCIL shares of Re 1, with SHRL to be listed on BSE and NSE; TCIL's own shareholding pattern is unchanged except for accelerated ESOP shares.
points.quote: SHRL shall issue and allot 81 (Eighty One) fully paid up equity shares of face value of Rs. 10 each for every 100 (One Hundred) fully paid up equity shares of Re. 1 each to the equity shareholders of TCIL ,

points.point: Indicative post-scheme SHRL ownership mirrors TCIL: 65.55% promoters (including 7% retained by TCIL), 2.16% ESOP trust and 32.30% public, with 65,70,000 ESOP 2024 options accelerated before Record Date 1.
points.quote: SHRL is presently a wholly owned subsidiary of TCIL . Pursuant to the effectiveness of the Demerger , each shareholder of TCIL , subject to applicable law, will be issued equity shares of SHRL in the ratio of 81 shares for every 100 shares held in TCIL .

points.point: The share-capital consolidation (4 Re-1 shares into 1 Rs-4 share, 47,69,50,562 shares becoming 11,92,37,641) is justified as improving key financial ratios so the market price better reflects intrinsic value and signals financial stability — expected within 15-18 months of Board approval.
points.quote: The Board of TCIL believes that the proposed consolidation of the face value of its equity shares will result in an improvement in certain key financial ratios.

points.point: The merger leg removes three shell entities — TC Visa Services (India), Jardin Travel Solutions and Borderless Travel Services, all with nil or negligible turnover (TCVSL Rs 1.2 crore, the others nil, versus TCIL's Rs 2,243.97 crore) — purely to cut compliance and overhead.
points.quote: TCVSL , JTSL and BTSL are dormant and non -operative companies, incurring unnecessary compliance and administrative costs.

points.point: A further capital reduction cuts TCIL's face value from Rs 4 to Rs 3 per share with no payment to shareholders and no change in share count, so proportionate holdings stay intact.
points.quote: The face value of paid -up equity shares of TCIL will be reduced from Rs. 4/- (Indian Rupees Four Only) per equity share to Rs. 3/- (Indian Rupees Three Only) per equity share , without any payment to the shareholders of TCIL.

verdict.what_management_expects: TCIL: streamlined capital structure, resources concentrated on core Travel and Financial Services, simpler corporate structure and higher EPS from face-value consolidation plus dormant-subsidiary merger, and ratios that better reflect intrinsic value. Sterling/SHRL: own growth path as a listed hospitality player, 34-36% EBITDA margins, stronger operating leverage, rising cash generation, disciplined capital allocation. Both: better focus, improved operational efficiencies and profitability, and unlocked shareholder value.
verdict.gaps: No basis for the 81:100 ratio or Sterling's standalone financials/valuation; no debt, float or asset allocation between entities; no reason for the Rs 4-to-Rs 3 reduction, lender or partner consents, or why 2026 not 2024.

verdict.rationale: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise (the Demerged Company) today runs three verticals — Healthcare Services (hospitals), Apollo HealthCo (omnichannel pharmacy and digital health) and AHLL (diagnostics and primary care) — and is carving the omnichannel pharmacy/digital health business (the 'Identified Business Undertaking', carried on directly and through Apollo Healthco Ltd, 'Transferor Company 1') into a separately listed Resultant Company, referred to on the May 2026 call as Apollo Healthtech. Management confirmed in Aug 2025 that 'Apollo HealthCo., as you are seeing in the current form' is what gets demerged and listed, as part of a composite scheme that simultaneously amalgamates Keimed (Transferor Company 2) and AHL into the new entity, consolidating pharmacy distribution in 'an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution.' The stated problem is strategic mismatch: the board says the business is 'distinct from other businesses undertaken by Demerged Company, and necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory,' so separation enables focus, efficient management and control, cost rationalization, streamlined statutory compliances and economies of scale for both sides. The capital-markets motive is explicit in the filing — the Resultant Company is to 'build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders' — i.e. a vehicle with its own shareholder base rather than a pharmacy/digital business funded inside a hospital company. Operationally they cite supply-chain integration, higher availability and larger assortment, and improved supply-chain transparency 'preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines.' The numbers management attached: a combined-entity run rate of INR 25,000 crore of revenue at 7% EBITDA (Feb 2026), Apollo HealthCo crossing INR 10,000 crore of annual revenue for the first time in FY26, a 3,200-crore GMV target with digital breakeven targeted in Q4 (Aug 2025), and management's view that 'the biggest lift' to EBITDA comes once the digital business breaks even. Incentive alignment is also built in: an Upside Agreement dated June 30, 2025 under which Rasmeli shares part of its investment upside with the AHL Promoter (Shobana Kamineni) and identified AHL employees 'in order to incentivise the management,' plus a reconstituted board (AHL Promoter, 3 Resultant-Company-promoter nominees, 1 AHEL nominee, 1 Rasmeli nominee, 6 independent directors).
verdict.evolution: By the Aug 2025 call the structure was already decided and analysts were asking for mechanics: Raman KV mapped the three segments and A. Krishnan confirmed Apollo HealthCo in its then-current form would be demerged and listed, with Keimed merging in for pharmacy synergies; the underlying Upside Agreement is dated June 30, 2025. By Feb 2026 the story had shifted from design to regulatory execution plus a hard financial target — CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NCLT filed and hearings begun, Keimed's subsidiary network streamlined into 100% subsidiaries, and a stated combined run rate of INR 25,000 crore revenue at 7% EBITDA. In May 2026 management reframed it as a completed-year 'strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business' for 'unlocking long-term value', set the NCLT-convened shareholder meeting for June 24, and reaffirmed (unchanged, 'as planned earlier') listing of Apollo Healthtech by end-December/early Q4 FY27, by which point the entity should show INR 25,000 crore of annualized revenue. Across the three calls the rationale itself never changed; only the timetable, approvals and the revenue milestones hardened.

points.point: Analyst Raman KV laid out the three-segment structure (hospitals, Apollo HealthCo pharmacy, AHLL diagnostics/primary care) and asked whether the pharmacy business was being demerged; A. Krishnan confirmed Apollo HealthCo in its current form is what gets demerged and listed.
points.quote: What will happen is Apollo HealthCo., as you are seeing in the current form, is what is going to be demerged and will be list

points.point: The analyst explicitly asked how the Keimed merger creates synergy for the pharmacy business, i.e. the combination rationale was being probed by investors from the start.
points.quote: And can you also explain , - how will the merger with Keimed Health be beneficial in terms of synergy for the pharmacy business?

points.point: Management reaffirmed the digital/pharmacy operating targets underpinning the separated entity: GMV of 3,200 on course per AOP, diagnostics at a 'new normal', and breakeven on course for Q4, with gross margin about 340 bps higher in Q1 vs Q4.
points.quote: So, the GM V of 3,200 that we spoke about, we continue to be on course.

points.point: Management tied the composite scheme (Keimed merger + Apollo HealthCo demerger) to a specific scale outcome for the combined entity: INR 25,000 crore of combined revenue at 7% EBITDA.
points.quote: We have also made progress with respect to the regulatory integration process for the com posite scheme of Keimed merger and demerger of Apollo HealthCo and remain well positioned to capture the full benefits of scale with the combined entity to achieve a run rate of INR 25,000 crore in combined revenues with 7% EBITDA.

points.point: Obul Reddy gave the regulatory status: CCI and SEBI approvals obtained, NCLT filing made and hearings started, with the next step awaited.
points.quote: We have obtained Competition Commission approval and SEBI approval. We have filed with NCLT.

points.point: On the pre-condition that Keimed buy out associates holding stakes in the separate pieces, management said Keimed is on time and has consolidated the structure into wholly owned subsidiaries.
points.quote: Keimed has progressing on time and Keimed has streamlined the entire subsidiary network, and they are 100% subsidiaries

points.point: Management characterised the transaction in its own words as a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business aimed at sharpening focus and unlocking long-term value across the integrated platform.
points.quote: During the year, we also announced a strategic restructuring of the omnichannel pharmacy and digital health business, an important step towards sharpening focus on unlocking long -term value across our integrated health care platform.

points.point: Timeline reaffirmed: NCLT-convened shareholder meeting on June 24, demerger completion targeted by Q4 FY27, unchanged from the earlier plan.
points.quote: The NCLT convened meeting of the shareholders is now being called for on June 24 to obtain the requisite shareholder approval, consequent to which we are hopeful the demerger process is completed by Q4 FY27 as planned earlier.

points.point: Scale milestones cited for the business being separated: consolidated revenue crossed INR 25,000 crore (INR 25,229 crore) for the first time and Apollo HealthCo alone passed INR 10,000 crore in annual revenue, after Healthcare Services did so in FY25.
points.quote: Apollo HealthCo also surpassed INR 10,000 crore in annual revenues for the first time following a similar milestone achieved by our Healthcare Services business in FY25.

points.point: A. Krishnan named the listed entity and the listing window, and said it should show INR 25,000 crore of annualized revenue by that quarter.
points.quote: And hopefully, by Q4 FY27, end of December or early Q4 FY27 is when Apollo Healthtech should get demerged and listed.

points.point: Management said the decisive earnings driver for the separated entity is digital breakeven, with store/distribution maturation already visible and the cost structure supporting the growth; they claim to be on course versus published pro forma.
points.quote: But I think the biggest lift will come the moment the digital business breaks even and then starts contributing to the EBITDA story because if you have to look at the cost structure that is something which is reasonably and this growth should be able to su stain that.

points.point: The core board rationale: the Identified Business Undertaking is distinct from AHEL's other businesses and needs its own strategy for its industry-specific risks and growth trajectory, so both companies can focus, manage and control efficiently.
points.quote: The Scheme would enable carving-out of the Identified Business Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) , which is distinct from other businesses undertaken by Demerged Company, and necessitates a differentiated strategy aligned to its industry specific risks, market dynamics, and growth trajectory.

points.point: The scheme consolidates the pharmacy distribution businesses of AHL (Transferor Company 1) and Keimed (Transferor Company 2) into one independent company focused exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution.
points.quote: The Scheme would also result in consolidation of pharmacy distribution business of Transferor Company 1 and Transferor Company 2, in an independent company focusing exclusively on digital health and pharmacy distribution, enabling synergies;

points.point: The explicit capital-markets purpose: a separate vehicle able to raise a wider capital and financial base by attracting a different investor, partner and lender set — the clearest statement of who the separation is for.
points.quote: The Scheme is expected to enable Resultant Company to build a wider capital and financial base, by attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and stakeholders, as well as promoting overall business growth;

points.point: Operating benefits claimed include supply-chain integration with higher availability and larger assortment, and supply-chain transparency that keeps counterfeit or substandard medicines out of the ecosystem.
points.quote: Improved transparency in the supply chain preventing the entry of counterfeit or substandard medicines into the ecosystem;

points.point: Management incentives are embedded via the June 30, 2025 Upside Agreement: Rasmeli shares part of its investment upside with the AHL Promoter (Shobana Kamineni) and identified AHL employees, with the obligation re-linked to Rasmeli's shareholding in the Resultant Company.
points.quote: Rasmeli has agreed to share an agreed portion of the upside received by it (and its affiliates) pursuant to its investment into Transferor Company 1 with the AHL Promoter and the identified employees of Transferor Company 1 (or any successor entity), its (existing and future) subsidiaries and (existing and future) associate companies, in order to incentivise the management of such companies.

points.point: Governance of the new entity is pre-set: board of AHL Promoter, three Resultant-Company-promoter nominees, one AHEL nominee, one Rasmeli nominee and six independent directors; a rights issue of 9,95,50,000 shares for INR 19,91,00,000 is also provided for.
points.quote: Upon the Scheme becoming effective, the board of directors of Resultant Company shall be reconstituted as follows: (i) AHL Promoter; (ii) 3 (three) directors nominated by the Resultant Company Promoters; (iii) 1 (one) director nominated by Demerged Company; (iv) 1 (one) director nominated by Rasmeli; and (v) 6 (six) independent directors.

verdict.what_management_expects: Resultant Company (Apollo Healthtech): a pure digital-health and pharmacy-distribution vehicle at ~INR 25,000 crore annualized revenue and 7% EBITDA, with its own investors, partners and lenders, supply-chain integration, cost rationalization, scale economies, and EBITDA lift once digital breaks even. AHEL: focus on hospitals plus AHLL, sharper managerial and board attention, and long-term value unlocked across the platform.
verdict.gaps: No share entitlement ratio, valuation, debt or working-capital allocation, royalty/brand or supply agreements between entities, post-demerger hospital margins, Rasmeli's economics, or who first demanded separation.

verdict.rationale: The supplied texts do not describe a separation, demerger or spin-off at all: the scheme filing is an amalgamation (absorption) of a subsidiary — the Transferor Company — into Ambuja Cements Ltd., the Transferee Company, and no business is being carved out. The stated starting point is ownership: the Transferee is already the promoter of the Transferor, holding 58.08% of its paid-up equity share capital (as on June 30, 2025) and 100% of its 8% non-convertible cumulative redeemable preference shares, and both are part of the Adani Group. Because 'both the companies are under the same line of business,' management argues the merger lets Ambuja 'absorb the business of Transferor Company completely for carrying on more effectively and beneficially.' The operating case given is integration economics: better resource utilization, reduced overheads, cost savings, economies of scale, elimination of duplicated efforts and streamlined compliance, plus 'reduction and rationalisation of multiple entities in the group.' The value case is stated only generically — enhanced business potential of the Transferor, value added to both companies and increased shareholders' value — with no margin, synergy-rupee or capacity figures in the rationale section. A second, distinct purpose is governance/shareholding: on effectiveness, certain Promoters/Promoter Group/related persons of the Transferor are to be reclassified from 'Promoter and Promoter Group' to 'Public' in the Transferee under SEBI LODR Regulation 31A, on the stated basis that they will not hold more than ten percent of total voting rights, exercise no direct or indirect control, hold no special rights or shareholder agreements, have no board seat or nominee director, are not KMP, and are neither wilful defaulters nor fugitive economic offenders. Process support is documented rather than argued: two valuation reports dated December 17, 2024 (BDO Valuation Advisory LLP for the Transferor; GT Valuation Advisors Private Limited for the Transferee) with fairness opinions from Vivro Financial Services (Transferor) and IDBI Capital Markets & Securities (Transferee), unanimous approval by both boards on December 17, 2024 (6 directors at the Transferor, 8 at the Transferee, including Gautam Adani as Chairman), NSE as Designated Stock Exchange, no-objection applications to the exchanges on January 3, 2025, and complaint reports to BSE (March 6, 2025) and NSE (March 25, 2025, updated June 16, 2025). Nothing in the texts attributes the transaction to a request from investors, lenders or partners.
verdict.evolution: The only tagged call material is February 2026 (transcript header: January 30, 2026), and it contains no mention of any separation, demerger or amalgamation — the Q&A with Rajesh Ravi of HDFC Securities covers clinker commissioning and prior-period tax refunds only, so no call-by-call evolution of the idea can be traced from these texts. verdict.rationale: Astral Limited says it has grown into two distinct verticals — (a) Plumbing: pipes, fittings, water tanks, faucets and sanitaryware, and (b) Chemicals: adhesives, polyvinyl acetate (PVA), cyanoacrylates, solvent cements, silicone sealants, epoxy resins, construction chemicals, putties and allied products, further scaled into specialty chemicals through recent strategic acquisitions. The Board (approval dated June 25, 2026) adopted a Composite Scheme that (i) demerges the Chemicals/Chemical Undertaking of Astral Limited (the Demerged Company) on a going-concern basis into Astral Chemie Limited, formerly Astral Coatings Private Limited, a 100% subsidiary that already manufactures and supplies paints and coatings for residential, commercial and industrial end-users, and (ii) amalgamates Al-Aziz Plastics Private Limited, another 100% subsidiary making electrofusion fittings, compression fittings, saddles, electrical fittings and allied accessories for gas, water, electricity and solar distribution/transmission, into Astral Limited because it is complementary to the Plumbing Business. The size cited: the Demerged Undertaking's turnover for the year ended March 31, 2026 was ₹12,663 million, 21% of the Demerged Company's total turnover, against Astral Limited's standalone FY26 turnover of ₹59,076 million and net worth of ₹41,058 million; Al-Aziz was small at ₹373 million turnover and ₹215 million net worth. The stated problems it solves: each business has different products, customer segments, operating models, capital requirements, risk profiles and growth opportunities and operates under different macroeconomic environments, regulatory frameworks and market risks, so one corporate roof blurred focus — the demerger puts chemicals plus paints under a single dedicated platform run by a focused leadership team with deep sector-specific expertise, and isolates the operational, cyclical and compliance risks of each business. It is also framed as a capital-structure fix: each entity can independently determine capex, working capital, funding and investment strategy based on its own growth prospects, capital intensity, cash-flow profile and risk-return characteristics, and as separately listed entities both can independently access debt and equity capital and attract strategic and financial investors with different investment objectives. For Al-Aziz, the added reasons are integration of its manufacturing facilities, products and customer relationships with Plumbing, plus reduced legal and regulatory compliance burden and administrative costs. Mechanics are value-neutral to holders: no cash consideration, 1 equity share of Astral Chemie (₹1 face value) for every 1 Astral share (₹1 face value), a mirrored shareholding pattern (promoters 54.22%, public 45.78% post-Scheme versus 100% promoter-held pre-Scheme), Astral's existing shares in Astral Chemie cancelled, no change in Astral's own shareholding, and listing sought on NSE and BSE.
verdict.evolution: The reasoning cannot be traced call by call from the material supplied: the only earnings-call passage provided is [May 2025], and it is entirely about end-market sizing — PVC at about 4.5 million tons in fiscal 25, CPVC at roughly 2.5 lakh tons or about 5% of PVC, and fire-sprinkler pipes as the next leg of CPVC demand — with no mention of a demerger, of the chemicals vertical, or of Astral Coatings/Astral Chemie. The separation therefore appears in these texts only at the Board approval of the Composite Scheme on June 25, 2026, sized off FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) financials, by which point Astral Coatings Private Limited had already been renamed Astral Chemie Limited and the chemicals portfolio had been expanded 'through recent strategic acquisitions' into specialty chemicals — the one hint of a build-up preceding the announcement. One drafting shift is visible inside the filing itself: the rationale annexure and disclosure tables describe the demerger of the 'Chemical Undertaking'/'Chemicals Business Undertaking', while the press-release text describes 'the demerger of its Adhesive Business', a narrower label for the same undertaking.

verdict.rationale: Astra Microwave Products Limited (AMPL) is demerging its Space, Meteorology and Hydrology business into its wholly owned subsidiary Astra Space Technologies Private Limited (ASTPL), leaving AMPL as a Radar Electronics, Electronic Warfare and Telemetry focused entity — i.e. two sector-focused listed entities. Management framed the core problem as a conglomerate of unlike businesses under one roof: the company does design, development and manufacture of RF and microwave sub-systems across defence, space, meteorology and telecommunication, and the Space/Meteorology/Hydrology piece 'operates in a sector with distinct industry characteristics, competitive dynamics, regulatory environment, and risk profile, necessitating a differentiated growth strategy.' The separated unit is small relative to the parent: turnover of roughly INR 157 crores for FY ended 31 March 2026, 13.58% of total turnover (against group turnover of INR 1157 crores for FY26), so it was arguably starved of dedicated management attention inside a defence-led parent guiding 15–20% FY27 top-line growth. The stated fixes are sharper strategic and operational focus, dedicated management teams pursuing sector-specific growth opportunities, enhanced governance and accountability, a simplified corporate structure, and clearer investment propositions for shareholders. The filing is explicit that a standalone space entity 'would be better positioned to attract investors, strategic partners, lenders, and other stakeholders with sector-specific interests' — the demand cited is from capital providers and partners generally, not any named investor or lender. Mechanically it is a mirror demerger: 1 ASTPL share of INR 2 for every 1 AMPL share of INR 2, no cash consideration, ASTPL's existing 100% promoter-held capital cancelled, post-scheme shareholding 6.45% promoters / 93.55% public, to be listed on BSE and NSE, subject to NCLT, SEBI and exchange approvals. Management also tied the move to capitalizing on emerging opportunities in India and globally, and to value unlocking for shareholders.
verdict.evolution: In the passages supplied, the idea appears only at the Jun 2026 call (transcript dated May 27, 2026), where the Board had given in-principle approval to demerge the space, meteorology and hydrology business and management said the detailed scheme would be shared 'once it is formally approved by board, which is expected over the next few weeks.' That promise was kept on the stated timeline: the Board approved the Scheme of Arrangement on 10 June 2026, on the recommendation of the Independent Directors Committee and Audit Committee, with the filing dated 10.06.2026. So the only observable evolution is in-principle approval plus a qualitative rationale in May 2026, hardening weeks later into a formal scheme with the resulting entity named (ASTPL), the perimeter defined, turnover quantified (INR 157 crores / 13.58%), and a 1:1 share entitlement ratio. No earlier call passages discussing the separation were provided, so nothing can be said from these texts about whether the idea surfaced before May 2026.

verdict.rationale: Anant Raj Limited says it today runs two distinct verticals — a real estate business and a data centre and cloud services business (the "Data Centre Business") — and that the Data Centre Business is currently split across two entities, ARL itself and its wholly owned subsidiary Anant Raj Cloud Private Limited (ARCPL), with assets, employees, investments and operations housed across both. That fragmentation is the specific problem the composite scheme fixes: step one merges ARCPL into ARL, step two demerges the resulting Demerged Undertaking into Ashok Cloud Private Limited (ACPL), so the entire data centre and cloud business sits in a single dedicated corporate entity and becomes a separate listed company. Management's stated reason is that the two businesses now have different growth drivers, capital requirements and operating models, and that the Data Centre Business 'has evolved significantly' and is ready to chart its own growth path while still leveraging ARL's institutional strengths, brand equity and goodwill. The filing's financials frame the asymmetry: for FY ended 31 March 2026, ARL turnover ₹1,491.52 crore and net worth ₹4,471.64 crore; ARCPL turnover ₹136.20 crore and net worth ₹49.45 crore; ACPL, the resultant company, turnover ₹0.00 crore and net worth ₹0.04 crore, with paid-up capital of ₹71.98 crore (ARL), ₹2.50 crore (ARCPL) and ₹74.91 crore (ACPL). The claimed benefits are five: two focused businesses with dedicated management teams; unlocking value via independent market recognition of the cloud business as a pure-play digital infrastructure company; direct shareholder participation through a 1:1 share entitlement (one ₹2 ACPL share per ₹2 ARL share held); a simplified structure with streamlined governance, greater transparency and faster decision-making; and greater flexibility for the cloud business to attract sector-focused investors, strategic partnerships, acquisitions and growth capital. Post-restructuring ARL stays focused on real estate and infrastructure while Ashok Cloud builds data centre, colocation, sovereign public cloud and AI-ready cloud infrastructure. Notably, ARL's existing shareholding in ACPL is not cancelled, so ACPL remains a subsidiary of ARL even after the demerger.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied with this prompt — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so there is no call-by-call trail to reconstruct and nothing can be said about how the idea surfaced or changed across three years of calls without going outside the texts given. The only dated evidence here is the board meeting of July 21, 2026 (commenced 4:30 P.M., concluded 6:15 P.M.), at which the Board, on the recommendation of the Independent Directors and the Audit Committee, approved the Composite Scheme of Arrangement under sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013. Within that single document the plan is already a two-step composite structure (ARCPL merged up into ARL, then the data centre undertaking demerged down into ACPL) rather than a simple spin-off, which is itself the response to the business being housed across two entities.

verdict.rationale: Across these texts the "separation" is really one composite scheme with two legs: a demerger out of Wim Plast Limited (WPL) and the amalgamation of WimPlast into Cello World Limited (CWL), with Cello Consumer Products Private Limited (CCPPL) as the third party to the scheme — per the filing, WPL shareholders receive CWL equity "pursuant to the demerger and the amalgamation, in accordance with Clause 8.1 and Clause 16.1 of the Scheme, respectively." On the November 13, 2024 call, Gaurav Rathod gave exactly two rationales for folding WimPlast back in: first, "we do not see any point in running 2 separate listed entities as the business is not very different"; second, WimPlast's manufacturing footprint "in different parts of the country" can be shared with Cello's other plastic product lines. Management framed the standalone listing as the problem being solved — "standing outside was not making sense, and that's the reason that the merger is happening" — and explicitly ruled out any further break-up of Cello's three verticals, arguing furniture manufacturing "is very, very similar to our other plastic manufactured products." Housekeeping consequences management confirmed: WimPlast first becomes a 100% subsidiary of CWL, WimPlast's ~8% loan to Cello World is extinguished in the merger, and WimPlast shareholders get 86 CWL shares (per the analyst's restatement, which Rathod confirmed). The filing adds the mechanics: NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned the scheme on May 14, 2026, the Board set May 27, 2026 as Effective Date with Appointed Date April 1, 2025 and June 09, 2026 as Record Date, and WPL's authorised capital combines into CWL's, reclassified to INR 140 crore (28 crore shares of INR 5). On the call tagged Jun 2026 (held May 29, 2026), management reported the scheme effective and FY26 comparatives restated from the beginning of the prior year, alongside FY26 revenue growth of 8.8%, EBITDA of INR526.4 crores (22.7% margin), PAT of INR331.5 crores (14.3% margin), CFO of INR255.1 crores, debt-to-equity of 0.01, capex of INR219 crores (steel bottle line, select consumerware, writing instruments, maintenance) and FY27 capex guidance of ~INR100 crores. No investor, lender or partner is named anywhere as having demanded the restructuring — the only pressure visible is analyst questioning, including Karan's observation that WimPlast traded at 10–12 PE against Cello World's ~60 PE, which management did not engage with as a rationale.
verdict.evolution: By the November 13, 2024 call the merger was already announced and management said it had "previously mentioned this as well," so the origin pre-dates these passages; that call is where the two rationales, the 100% subsidiary step, the 8% intercompany loan and the 86-share entitlement were spelled out under questioning from Deepesh Sancheti (Manya Financial Services) and Karan. Also in Nov 2024, management closed the door on the logical extension — demerging the three unrelated-looking verticals — on synergy grounds, so the direction of travel was consolidation, not separation. The plan then executes rather than changes: NCLT Ahmedabad sanctions it May 14, 2026, the Board declares it effective May 27, 2026 (Appointed Date April 1, 2025; Record Date June 09, 2026), and on the May 29, 2026 call (tagged Jun 2026) management reports completion plus restated comparatives and pending EPS impact. Nothing in these texts shows the rationale itself being revised, re-scoped or re-priced between 2024 and 2026.

points.point: Asked directly for the rationale, Rathod gave two: running two separate listed entities made no sense given similar businesses, and WimPlast's plants across the country can be shared with Cello's other plastic lines.
points.quote: So, I think, we previously mentioned this as well, there are 2 rationales, one is that there s - we do not see any point in running 2 separate listed entities as the business is not very different.

points.point: The second rationale was explicitly manufacturing-asset sharing across geographies, not cost savings quantified in rupees.
points.quote: Secondly, there is a lot of manufacturing facilities that WimPlast has, so in different parts of the country wherein we can share manufacturing facilities with our other plastic product lines.

points.point: Management ruled out demerging Cello's three verticals, saying the merger itself proves the opposite intent and that furniture shares manufacturing with other plastic products.

verdict.rationale: Management (Vishal Mehta) framed the separation as making the listed entity a pure payments company and pushing non-payment assets out of the payments regulatory perimeter: asked directly for the rationale on the Aug 2024 call, he said "we are a payments company," that "with a lot of regulations, we believe that digital marketing will be decoupled from payments," and that digital marketing has "a much larger ecosystem" it can address once separated. The business being carved out is ODigMa, the digital-marketing arm, sized at about INR30 crores of annual revenue and less than INR1 crore of annual profitability — i.e. small on revenue and immaterial on profit, which is why management could treat the revenue impact as minor. A second asset cited was the .OOO ("dot triple O") top-level domain, which they admitted they had "not been able to build up a lot of monetization" on inside the company, implying it needs a different owner/vehicle. The mechanism was a composite scheme of arrangement: filed and awaiting regulators as of Nov 2023, NCLT-approved by Nov 2024 with shares allotted to shareholders and a listing-and-trading application pending with the exchanges. Management drew a deliberate line around AI: Phronetic/the AI vertical was put into a separate company for talent reasons ("AI is definitely a separate company, such a talent tool") but explicitly NOT demerged, because it is a platform with "a lot of synergies between what Phronetic is building out on video intelligence and payments" that they want to build and keep. The retained-side logic was also brand/ecosystem: CCAvenue is the B2B, business-facing brand and the acquired Rediff is the consumer-facing brand, giving them "an ecosystem to target both" for payments and financial products (express settlement at a $600 million run rate, bill payments, recharges, tax payments). The cost side was acknowledged in Feb 2025 — one-time legal costs for demergers plus Rediff advertising/bandwidth costs hitting PAT, with management stating they are "not optimizing for PAT" but for growth and cash flows. Shareholder pressure is visible as context rather than as a stated cause: investors pointed to EPS below INR1, a share price "stagnant since many quarters," consistent insider selling and absent institutional investors; no lender or commercial partner is cited anywhere as requesting the separation.
verdict.evolution: By the Nov 2023 call the demerger was already filed and simply waiting on regulators, with no rationale given — the only framing was an investor's hope that EPS would rise above INR1. On the Aug 2024 call the content appears: ODigMa is named and sized (INR30 crores revenue, <INR1 crore profit), the rationale is articulated as regulatory decoupling of digital marketing from payments plus the unmonetized .OOO top-level domain, and the question widens to whether the AI vertical will also be demerged — answered as "set up as a separate company for now" but no demerger commitment. By Nov 2024 execution is largely done (NCLT approval, shares allotted, exchange listing application pending) and management firmly rules out a near-term Phronetic AI demerger in favour of building it for payments synergies, while investors shift to complaining about stagnant price and insider selling; Feb 2025 only adds that demerger legal costs are a one-time drag. The filing-era documents show the restructuring continued past the calls: the Platform Business Undertaking was slump-sold to subsidiary Rediff.com India Limited, leaving standalone operations in a single Payment Business segment, alongside a rights-issue object variation, a 10:1 share consolidation and the rename to AvenuesAI Limited.

points.point: The demerger was already filed with regulators and management offered no rationale at this stage — only a status update and a promise to revert once regulators respond.
points.quote: We filed for the demerger. So we expect to hear back from the regulators. But as soon as we hear back, we will update you on the same.

points.point: Shareholder context for the restructuring: an individual investor tied his expectations to EPS, which was then below INR1, and management promised to work toward it.
points.quote: We are waiting that our EPS will be increased because it's now below INR1.

points.point: On the core business management refused margin-percentage targets, saying the focus is absolute cash generation in a competitive (non-monopoly) market where they are among the top three in India.
points.quote: So we think that as far as our business is concerned, let's focus on the absolute cash generation and not just percentages while we keep on working on the operating metrics that will help us improve our margins.

points.point: Asked for ODigMa's size, management quantified the demerged digital-marketing business at roughly INR30 crores of annual revenue with under INR1 crore of annual profitability.
points.quote: ODigMa will be about INR30 crores. And about profitability would be about -- I mean these are annual numbers, and profitability will be about less than INR1 crore.

points.point: The stated rationale, given in answer to a direct question: as a payments company under heavy regulation, digital marketing must be decoupled from payments and can then address a far larger ecosystem.
points.quote: With a lot of regulations, we believe that digital marketing will be decoupled from payments. And there's a much larger ecosystem that digital marketing can attend into.

points.point: The second limb of the rationale was the .OOO top-level domain, which management conceded they had not been able to monetize meaningfully within the company.
points.quote: Second is that we have a domain called dot triple O.

points.point: The AI vertical was deliberately treated differently: housed in a separate company mainly as a talent vehicle and an investment bet, with pilots completed and a partial second-phase rollout, but with no demerger commitment.
points.quote: And we think that while we may not have an answer for you in terms of demerger, but it's definitely set up as a separate company for now.

points.point: Retained-side logic: CCAvenue stays the B2B brand while the acquired Rediff supplies a consumer-facing brand, letting financial products be sold to both businesses and consumers; express settlement was cited at a $600 million run rate.
points.quote: CCAvenue is business-facing brand, B2B, and Rediff is a consumer-facing brand.

points.point: Execution update: the composite scheme of arrangement had been approved by NCLT, shares allotted to shareholders, and a listing-and-trading application was pending with the exchanges.
points.quote: So in other words, we believe that NCLT has approved the composite scheme of arrangement. Shares have been allocated to the respective shareholders and the company has filed an application with the exchanges for the approval of listing and trading.

points.point: Management explicitly declined to extend the demerger logic to Phronetic AI, saying it is a platform serving all businesses with direct synergies to payments that they intend to build and keep.
points.quote: And there's a lot of synergies between what Phronetic is building out on video intelligence and payments.

points.point: Investor framing after the first demerger: despite new businesses and rising revenue, the share price was stagnant with insider selling and no institutional participation.
points.quote: But share price performance is stagnant since many quarters, with consistent selling coming from insiders.

points.point: The separation carried one-time costs — demerger legal fees plus new advertising and bandwidth charges from the Rediff acquisition — which management said would hit PAT, a metric they are not optimizing for.
points.quote: So there are certain legal costs for demergers.

points.point: The filing documents a further separation beyond the calls: the Platform Business Undertaking was transferred on a going-concern basis by slump sale to subsidiary Rediff.com India Limited and is reported as discontinued operations.
points.quote: During the previous year, the Company had transferred its Platform Business Undertaking on a going concern basis through a slump sale to Rediff.com India Limited ("Rediff"), subsidiary of the Company.

points.point: Post-separation the standalone entity is a single-segment payments company — CCAvenue payment gateway, CPGS payment infrastructure for banks, and credit and lending.
points.quote: Accordingly, the Company now operates in a single business segment l.e. Payment Business which includes Payment Gateway business with CC Avenue business brand and payment infrastructure including CPGS towards banks, and Credit & Lending related business

points.point: Accompanying capital-structure actions approved by the Board: a 10-for-1 share consolidation (Re. 1 shares into Rs. 10 shares) alongside a variation in the objects of the June 19, 2025 rights issue.

verdict.what_management_expects: Payments stays the regulated core — CCAvenue, CPGS for banks, credit and lending, now a single standalone segment with Rediff adding a consumer brand beside B2B. Digital marketing (ODigMa, ~INR30cr revenue) is freed from payments regulation to chase a much larger ecosystem, with the unmonetized .OOO domain alongside it. Listed shares went directly to shareholders. Focus is cash generation, not PAT or margin percentages.
