verdict.rationale: These texts do not contain a stated rationale for separating a business, and no scheme of arrangement/demerger rationale section is present — the document labelled "Scheme Rationale" is in fact two SEBI LODR Regulation 30 disclosures by Coal India Ltd., neither of which gives reasons. The first (Ref. CIL:XI(D):4157/4156:2026:35185, dated 02.09.2026) discloses that the draft red herring prospectus dated 1st September 2026 of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL), a wholly owned subsidiary of CIL, was filed with SEBI, BSE and NSE, for a proposed IPO structured purely as an Offer for Sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares of face value INR 2 each held by Coal India Limited — i.e. a partial monetisation/listing of a producing coal subsidiary by the parent, not a demerger, and explicitly "subject to receipt of applicable approvals, prevailing market conditions, and other relevant considerations." No objects-of-the-issue, value-unlocking, focus, margin or capital-allocation reasoning is given, and no investor, lender or partner is named as having asked for it. The second (Ref. CIL:XID:04156/157:35043, dated 27.07.2026) is the opposite of a separation: CIL's Board approved investing in the rights issue of CIL Rajasthan Akshay Urja Limited (CRAUL), a renewable-energy JV with Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Urja Nigam Limited (RVUNL) incorporated 09.06.2025, with CIL subscribing 2,22,000 shares at Rs. 10 each (Rs. 22,20,000) and RVUNL 78,000 shares (Rs. 7,80,000), holding 74%/26%; paid-up capital Rs. 10,00,000 and size/turnover NIL, to develop solar, PSP and wind projects selling power to RVUNL under Section 62 of the Electricity Act, 2003 and to DISCOMs/third parties/C&I customers. The only call passage supplied (Feb 2024) runs directly against a separation thesis: asked whether renewables/alternative energy would be held as a separate demerged entity, management said the verticals already sit in existing subsidiaries and joint ventures, that no new subsidiary would be created, and that it "is not in our discussion right now"; the only numbers-adjacent remarks are that coal mine capex will be met from internal accruals, with little debt in FY25 but rising debt in the following year for renewal and gasification projects. On this evidence the correct answer is that CIL is not documented here as separating a business — it is listing a minority stake in MCL by Offer for Sale while continuing to fund renewables inside CIL's own subsidiary/JV structure.
verdict.evolution: Feb 2024 call: an investor (Venkatesh Subramanian) raised the idea unprompted, asking whether renewables/alternative energy would be carved out as a separate demerged entity; management rejected it, saying subsidiaries and JVs already exist, no new subsidiary would be created, and it was not under discussion. No 2025 or later call passages were provided, so there is no call-by-call progression toward a separation. The only later developments in these texts are corporate actions without commentary: the 27.07.2026 CRAUL rights-issue investment (keeping renewables in-house) and the 02.09.2026 disclosure of MCL's DRHP for an Offer-for-Sale IPO of CIL-held shares.

points.point: The separation idea came from an investor, not management — Venkatesh Subramanian asked whether the alternative/renewable energy business, alongside coal and CIL energy, would eventually be held as a separate demerged entity.
points.quote: And do you have any plans going forward once we have coal, we have CIL energy and then we have -- we're investing a lot in terms of alternative energy as well. Would you have that as a separate demerged entity or something in the future?

points.point: Management declined the demerger idea, saying renewable and other non-coal verticals are already housed in existing subsidiaries and joint ventures and that no new subsidiary was planned.
points.quote: We had already -- some verticals are there for the renewable energy and other projects, for that we had already subsidiaries companies are there.

points.point: Management stated explicitly that a separate demerged entity was not on the agenda at that time.
points.quote: We are not going to create any new subsidy. It is not in our discussion right now.

points.point: On funding, management confirmed coal mine capex would come from internal accruals with minimal debt in FY25, but flagged rising debt from the following year for mine renewal and coal gasification projects — the only capital-structure specifics given.

verdict.rationale: The separation is a demerger of the "Clinical Services" undertaking (the primary/secondary care clinics NHIC runs across Bengaluru) out of NH Integrated Care Private Limited (NHIC) and into the listed parent Narayana Hrudayalaya Limited (NHL), with an Appointed Date of April 1, 2025. Management's stated reason is that the clinics turned out not to be standalone: NHIC was incorporated to run primary and secondary care clinics "independently of hospital-based tertiary care services," but operational experience showed "substantial dependencies on hospital infrastructure" — consultant doctors and specialists primarily engaged at hospitals, advanced diagnostics "not viable at individual clinic locations," and patient pathways requiring tertiary care. Running clinics separately from hospitals forced duplicate administrative functions (finance, HR, procurement, IT, marketing), producing "increased costs, coordination inefficiencies, and the inability to realise economies of scale," and it crowded out NHIC's strategic priority, preventive healthcare. What stays behind in NHIC is Narayana Aarogyam, a preventive platform (health screening, risk assessment, wellness coaching, continuous monitoring) that is said to be structurally hospital-independent: dedicated technology-enabled testing centres, appointment-based services with no on-call specialists or emergency capability, minimal hospitalisation, and predictable resource needs — so it can go digital-first, AI-powered and asset-light, hire specialised digital health talent and pursue population-health partnerships. The filing cites "demonstrated investor interest in technology-enabled preventive healthcare platforms," plus lifestyle disease prevalence and corporate wellness mandates, as the growth case; no lender or partner demand is mentioned. The clinics being moved are small — Rs 39.94 crore of FY25 revenue, 1.11% of NHL's standalone turnover — and the mechanics are neutral: NHIC is already a wholly owned subsidiary, so there is no cash consideration, no share issuance, no change in shareholding and no new listing. On the June 2026 call Viren Shetty tied it directly to the clinic cash burn: sharing corporate overheads with the parent and "demerging the clinic business into the core" is how they expect to moderate costs while still expanding clinics, which they value as a patient feeder generating inpatient referrals for advanced therapies and future One Health insurance subscribers.
verdict.evolution: Of the passages supplied, the Feb 2026 call does not touch this transaction at all — it discusses a different restructuring, the UK Practice Plus carve-out (three legal entities, ~INR 40 crore depreciation for two months, with Sandhya J advising investors to wait for a full quarter). The clinic demerger first surfaces in the supplied material on the Jun 2026 call, where Viren Shetty mentions it almost in passing, as the answer to a question about continuing clinic cash burn: consolidation, shared corporate overheads with the parent, and "demerging the clinic business into the core." The scheme filing then formalises and broadens that same logic — hospital dependency, duplicated admin functions, value unlocking — and reframes the purpose around what remains in NHIC, the Aarogyam preventive healthcare platform, backdated to an Appointed Date of April 1, 2025 (i.e. before either call). No earlier call in the material contains the idea, so its origin and the preventive-healthcare framing appear only in the filing, not in the call record provided.

points.point: Viren Shetty frames the demerger as a cost/overhead fix: clinics move into the parent ("the core") so corporate overheads and resources are shared rather than duplicated, which is his answer to persistent clinic cash burn.
points.quote: What we are doing is a little bit of consolidation and a few of the corporate overheads can be worked in a way that we share resources with the parent and we'll be demerging the clinic business into the core that should help with a lot of that.

points.point: Management says clinic cash burn will continue at a similar run rate into the next year because they keep adding clinics, though fixed-cost leverage should moderate some of it — the pressure the restructuring is meant to relieve.
points.quote: So you have to assume that a similar run rate of cash burn will continue on the clinics going into next year as well because we still have a significant ambition in terms of growth of clinics in our core geographies.

points.point: The strategic justification for keeping clinics inside the hospital company: they reach domestic patients who would never otherwise come to Narayana, and feed inpatient referrals for advanced therapies and future One Health insurance customers.
points.quote: So they act as an excellent feeder for all the hospitals and build up that long -term relationship for patients who tomorrow will subscribe to our One Health plans insurance plans and then become Narayana Health customers.

points.point: This call addresses a separate restructuring, the UK Practice Plus carve-out, not the clinic demerger: Sandhya J explains that Practice Plus's old balance sheet covered three legal entities and the reported numbers are post-carve-out, with lease re-accounting agreed with the statutory auditors.
points.quote: So , the Practice Plus balance sheet was three legal entities which were there , and this is now after the carve out.

points.point: On the UK numbers (c. INR 40 crore depreciation for two months, per Slide 14), management tells investors the figures are usable going forward but to wait for a full quarter before treating them as representative.
points.quote: I would just recommend that you wait for Q4, where we get the full effect of all the numbers in our P&L.

points.point: Core operational reason: NHIC was set up to run clinics independently of hospital-based tertiary care, but experience showed the clinics depend on hospital-based specialists, hospital-grade diagnostics and tertiary care pathways.
points.quote: Operational experience has demonstrated  that the Demerged Undertaking has developed substantial dependencies on hospital infrastructure, particularly: (a) consultant doctors and specialists primarily engaged at hospital facilities; (b) advanced diagnostic services not viable at individual clinic locations; and (c) patient care pathways requiring tertiary care at hospital facilities.

points.point: Running clinics in a separate company duplicated finance, HR, procurement, IT and marketing, raising costs and blocking economies of scale, and distracted NHIC from its preventive healthcare priority.
points.quote: Separate operation of clinics and hospitals has necessitated duplicate administrative functions (finance, HR, procurement, IT, marketing), resulting in increased costs, coordination inefficiencies, and the inability to realise economies of scale.

points.point: Size and mechanics: the clinics being transferred had FY25 revenue of Rs 39.94 crore, 1.11% of NHL's standalone turnover; because NHIC is wholly owned, there is no cash, no share issue, no shareholding change and no new listing. Appointed Date is April 1, 2025.
points.quote: The turnover of the Clinical Services undertaking of the Demerged Company for the year ended March 31, 2025 was  Rs. 39.94 crore representing 1.11 % of the total standalone turnover of the Resulting Company for the year ended  March 31, 2025.

points.point: What remains in NHIC is Narayana Aarogyam — screening, risk assessment, wellness coaching and continuous monitoring — which is described as structurally independent of hospitals: appointment-based, no on-call specialists or emergency capability, minimal hospitalisation, predictable resource needs.
points.quote: Aarogyam operates independently of hospital infrastructure through: (a) dedicated technology-enabled preventive testing ce ntres; (b) scheduled appointment-based services without requiring on-call specialists or emergency capabilities; (c) minimal hospitalisation rates; and (d) predictable resource requirements without treatment-based operational variability.

points.point: Market/demand case, including the only reference to outside parties wanting this: investor appetite for technology-enabled preventive healthcare platforms, alongside lifestyle disease prevalence, corporate wellness mandates and digital health advances.
points.quote: The preventive healthcare sector presents  significant growth opportunities from lifestyle disease prevalence, corporate wellness mandates, technological advancements in digital health, and demonstrated investor interest in technology-enabled preventive healthcare platforms.

points.point: Post-demerger NHIC becomes a focused preventive-health company: digital-first and AI-powered, asset-light and scalable, with partnerships for population health management, and freedom to recruit specialised digital health expertise.
points.quote: Post-demerger, the Demerged Company will concentrate exclusively on developing the Aarogyam preventive healthcare platform through: (a) digital-first, AI-powered service delivery; (b) comprehensive screening and monitoring programs; (c) asset-light, scalable expansion; and (d) strategic partnerships for population health management.

points.point: Two different business models are being untangled — different value propositions, operating models, risk profiles, capital requirements and growth drivers — so each can run its own strategy.
points.quote: The Demerged Undertaking and Remaining Un dertaking represent distinct business models with materially different value propositions, operating models, risk profiles, capital requirements, and growth drivers.

points.point: Capital allocation is explicitly split: NHIC funds preventive healthcare technology without competing demands, while NHL funds clinic infrastructure off its own balance sheet.
points.quote: The Demerged Company can direct capital toward preventive healthcare technology investments without competing demands.  The Resulting Company will fund clinic infrastructure from its capital base.

points.point: Claimed benefits include value unlocking and better valuations, improved patient care coordination, clearer employee career paths, and cleaner governance/regulatory boundaries; NHL also gains unified care pathways and optimised specialist deployment.
points.quote: The Scheme will: (a) unlock value from distinct business segments and enable enhanced valuations; (b) improve patient care coordination and service quality;  (c) establish clearer organisational structur es and career paths for employees; and  (d) establish clear operational boundaries for governance and regulatory compliance.

verdict.what_management_expects: NHL: clinics folded into the core — unified care pathways, optimised specialist deployment, consolidated admin, procurement/IT/working-capital savings, overheads shared with the parent moderating clinic cash burn, plus a patient feeder into hospitals and One Health insurance. NHIC: pure preventive-care play on Aarogyam — sharper focus, digital/AI asset-light capital allocation, specialised hiring, ecosystem partnerships, value unlocked and "enhanced valuations" for both segments.

verdict.rationale: Management framed the separation as a value-unlocking restructuring: in the Nov 2023 call Arun Misra said the Board had approved demerging Vedanta Ltd. into six independent listed entities, 'each one capable of executing its individual business strategies,' with the scheme filed with the stock exchanges in October 2023 and described as creating 'six incredibly competitive, nimble and focused enterprises.' The scheme rationale gives the core logic: each demerged entity gets greater strategic flexibility, sharper market focus and independent access to capital, with management teams aligning decisions to customer needs, investment cycles and commodity-specific dynamics, while investors can 'evaluate and value each business on its own merits' — shareholders receive shares in proportion to existing holdings so ownership continuity is preserved. The resulting companies are Vedanta Aluminium (integrated aluminium, value-added and low-carbon), Vedanta Oil & Gas (via Malco Energy Ltd — India's largest private E&P), Vedanta Power (TSPL and other IPP assets), Vedanta Iron & Steel, and a base metals entity (Vedanta Base Metals Ltd), with the residual Vedanta Limited keeping the Hindustan Zinc stake and acting as 'an incubator for new and emerging businesses.' Chairman Anil Agarwal said each entity 'has the potential to grow manifold, attract strategic investment, and deliver superior value as these sectors are witnessing double digit growth,' and that the demerger is 'also about empowering leadership.' Management repeatedly tied it to scale and leadership depth — Aug 2024 cited '100-plus expats and experienced specialists' ready to run the separate businesses, and Nov 2024/Apr 2025 linked it to leadership in critical minerals and 'Vedanta 2.0' (global leader in critical minerals, energy transition and technology). Valuation was the explicit prize: in Nov 2024 Ajay Goel said 'there is a preponderance of opinion where everybody believes post-de-merger the value of the sums will be the parts will be more than the sum,' and promoter stake (VRL at 56.4% of VEDL) was expected to be worth more after the split. Creditors and regulators were active parties rather than requesters: the company was 'in talks with creditors for debt allocations' (Jan 2024), paid a Rs. 660 crore full-and-final SEPCO settlement 'as part of demerger proceedings' and a Rs. 1,248 crore bank guarantee to NCLAT over the TSPL demerger, and MoPNG/DGH objected over disputed Cairn dues. Throughout, the demerger was presented alongside deleveraging (VRL debt cut $3.7bn over two years, down to $5.5bn, targeting $3bn by 2027) and operating performance (FY25 revenue Rs. 150,725 crores, EBITDA Rs. 43,541 crores, net debt/EBITDA improved to 1.2x) as one of three priorities: 'business delivery, deleveraging, and demerger.'
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced as a board decision in the Nov 2023 call — six independent listed entities, scheme filed with exchanges in October 2023 — and the Jan 2024 call tracked approvals (exchange NOC passed to SEBI, awaiting SEBI NOC, creditor talks on debt allocation) while loosely describing a future 'portfolio of 17 pure-play companies.' Through Aug 2024 and Nov 2024 it moved to NCLT (first hearing done), with management calling it 'a final step,' stressing scheme flexibility to list each entity as its approval came, and guiding completion 'on or before 31st of March 2025.' Feb 2025 set the shareholder/creditor meeting for Feb 18, which voted in favour, after which Apr 2025 moved to the second motion petition with completion guided to September 2025; the Jul 2025 call slipped that to a Sept–Oct window amid an NCLAT interim stay on the TSPL power demerger and MoPNG objections over Cairn's disputed dues. By the Oct 2025 call the count had become five demerged entities with a final NCLT hearing on November 12 and listing targeted by end-FY26, the SEPCO dispute settled for Rs. 660 crores to clear the path; the NCLT order was pronounced 16.12.2025.

verdict.rationale: Triveni is executing a Composite Scheme of Arrangement approved by the Board on 10 December 2024 with two legs: the amalgamation of Sir Shadi Lal Enterprises (SSEL, a ~61.77%-owned subsidiary) into Triveni Engineering & Industries Ltd (TEIL), and the demerger of the Power Transmission Business (PTB) undertaking of TEIL into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd (TPTL), a wholly owned subsidiary that will be separately listed. On the SSEL leg, the scheme says both companies have sugar and distillery manufacturing verticals, so merging them consolidates all sugar, alcohol and ethanol operations into one entity, creating 'operational synergies, economies of scale, optimum utilization of resources,' eliminating duplication, cutting administrative and multi-entity compliance costs (statutory filings, labour law/establishment compliances) and improving the combined entity's 'competitive position and negotiating power.' On the PTB leg, the filing argues PTB and the Residual Business 'address different market segments with unique opportunities and dynamics in terms of business strategy, customer set, geographic focus, competition, capabilities set, talent needs and distinct capital requirements,' so separation lets each sharpen focus, improve competitiveness, operational efficiency and agility; PTB has 'attained a significant size, scale and has a large headroom for growth' and is 'entering the next phase of growth,' which the Board says warrants focused management attention; and because PTB has 'separate growth trajectories, risk profile and capital requirement,' segregation enables 'independent value discovery' and unlocking of value for each business. Tarun Sawhney framed it on the Feb 2025 call purely as 'value unlocking that the Board of Directors has felt very important,' and by Feb 2026 as being 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies.' The growth case was backed with capex: an incremental ₹60 crore approved in Feb 2025 on top of a ₹500 crore programme, taking gears capacity from ~₹400 crore today to ₹700 crore by September 2026, against a global high-speed and turbo gears market of only $650–700 million dominated by European gearbox makers, plus a Swiss subsidiary driving exports and qualification orders in oil and gas (pumps and compressors). Per the filing's FY2024-25 audited-accounts table, the demerger moves roughly ₹36,988.71 lakh of gross revenue and ₹13,693.93 lakh of EBITDA into TPTL (with a corresponding ₹36,689.32 lakh / ₹13,693.93 lakh reduction at TEIL), entitling TEIL shareholders to ONE ₹2 TPTL share for every THREE ₹1 TEIL shares, while SSEL holders get 100 TEIL shares for every 137 SSEL shares. The initiative was Board-driven, not demanded by lenders or partners; investors engaged mainly to contest the structure — Resham Jain of DSP Asset Managers argued the ~30% stake TEIL retains in TPTL means 'the same Holdco discount will be applicable,' to which Sawhney replied there were two reasons and that the Triveni Turbines precedent 'was actually quite a positive one for the Company.'
verdict.evolution: The scheme was announced on 10 December 2024 and first discussed with investors on the Feb 2025 call, where Sawhney laid out both legs, tied it to Board-led value unlocking, paired it with the ₹60 crore gears capex to ₹700 crore by September 2026, guided to NCLT approval 'by the end of this calendar year,' and defended the retained ~30% TPTL stake against Resham Jain's Holdco-discount objection. Through Jun 2025 and Aug 2025 the story became procedural and the timeline slipped — SEBI approval pending, then stock-exchange questions and 'another 30-odd days,' with completion pushed to Q1 of the next fiscal year, while investors asked for granular PTB disclosure ahead of separate listing and Sawhney began describing Board workshops on what the residual sugar/alcohol business does with its investable cash flows to regain 2022-23 margins. By Nov 2025 exchanges had approved and NCLT stakeholder meetings were set for end-November/early-December with culmination guided to Q4 FY26; the Feb 2026 call added the explicit purpose language 'to unlock value and to drive operational efficiencies,' confirmed shareholder and creditor approval in December 2025, and reported systems work so TPTL could 'hit the ground' as a standalone. On the Jun 2026 call Sawhney confirmed the scheme effective 19 May 2026 after NCLT approval, with appointed dates of 1 April 2025 (amalgamation) and 1 April 2026 (demerger), the SSEL record date of 3 June and the TEIL record date within four weeks, and CFO Suresh Taneja held PTB's ~35% PBIT as the go-forward trend.

verdict.rationale: The stated primary object is to consolidate all NBFC business of the two applicant companies into a single entity. The trigger is regulatory: Sammaan Capital Ltd (SCL), the listed company, was formerly registered with the National Housing Bank as a non-deposit-taking HFC (certificate dated December 28, 2005, registration number 02.0063.05), a licence later surrendered; following a shareholder resolution of September 25, 2023 and an application to RBI for conversion from HFC to NBFC-ICC, SCL received a certificate of registration dated June 28, 2024, number N-14.03624, under Section 45IA of the RBI Act, 1934, and RBI directed while issuing it that no other group entity shall hold an NBFC-ICC/HFC CoR within a prescribed timeline. Because Sammaan Finserve Ltd (SFL) — a wholly owned subsidiary that is itself an NBFC-ICC and is the Demerged Company here, with SCL as the Resulting Company holding its entire equity — also holds such a licence, the demerger transfers SFL's NBFC business to SCL on a going-concern basis to comply. Management argues the merged lending book gets a wider and stronger capital and asset base, pooled resources, knowledge and client relationships, a more diversified product suite on a unified platform, simpler corporate structure, economies of scale, lower administrative and compliance cost and a stronger risk-management architecture. The split also frees SFL, which says it is contemplating entry into the strategically distinct insurance broking and insurtech business and wants a dedicated management and operational structure for it, citing sustained insurance-industry growth, rising dependence on the broking channel, digital disruption, favourable regulatory reform and rising investor interest. Mechanically it is structured as a tax-neutral demerger under Section 2(19AA) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, with no shares issued as consideration since SCL already owns SFL fully, and NCD holders of SFL receiving one NCD of SCL for every one held on identical coupon, tenure, ISIN, redemption price, quantum and security.

Nothing in the supplied text describes how management first raised the idea publicly or how it changed.

verdict.rationale: Refex Industries Ltd. (RIL) is separating its green mobility (EV passenger transport) business from its core Ash & Coal handling business through a two-step composite scheme: first the amalgamation of its wholly owned subsidiary Refex Green Mobility Limited (RGML) into RIL, then the demerger of the Green Mobility Business Undertaking out of RIL into Refex Mobility Limited (RML), which will be independently listed parallel to RIL with mirror shareholding (no valuation exercise was required because RGML is a 100% subsidiary). The stated reason is structural dissimilarity: the scheme says the nature of risk and competition, financial profiles and return ratios of the Ash & Coal handling business are distinct from the Green Mobility Business, which is 'capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders.' Housing an asset-light, cash-generating ash/coal services business (management and an analyst put ash and coal at more than 96% of revenue; Anil Jain said standalone RIL will be 95–100% ash and coal) alongside a fleet business still building scale blurs both stories, so the scheme targets an 'independent global scale company' in mobility, greater management focus in each entity, the ability for investors to hold the two risk profiles separately, and 'focused and sharper capital market access (debt and equity).' Practically, RML takes roughly Rs.220 crores of net assets off RIL's consolidated balance sheet and, per Anil Jain, 'all the debt etc. will also move to that entity,' giving mobility 'more liberty to do its own business' and strategic and financial flexibility; RIL's results will no longer consolidate mobility. The separation sits inside a wider portfolio cleanup in the same period — a strategic call to exit power trading (wound up because 'the margins in power trading were extremely low and this was not in alignment' with the company's focus) and the refrigerant gas business, 'in order to achieve stronger return profiles by redeploying capital and focus towards core businesses.' Lenders are an explicit gating party: in January 2026 the company was 'waiting for some final NOCs from the lenders' before the scheme could be filed. Mobility itself is presented as credible standalone: over INR100 crores of revenue in three years of operation, improving utilization and unit economics, 'steadily progressing towards profitability.' Wind (Venwind Refex Power, Rs.1,860 crores cumulative order book) is explicitly not part of the separation and stays with RIL alongside ash and coal.
verdict.evolution: On the Nov 6, 2025 call the demerger first surfaced as an in-progress composite scheme, framed as unlocking 'focused value creation,' with management deflecting a valuation question (no valuation needed — 100% subsidiary, mirror shareholding) and noting mobility results would stop consolidating. By Jan 21, 2026 it had become concrete and conditional: final lender NOCs pending before filing, NCLT completion guided for end-April, Rs.220 crores of net assets and all mobility debt moving to RML, and RIL recast as a 95–100% ash-and-coal standalone, alongside the fresh decision to exit power trading and refrigerant gases. By the May 27, 2026 (Jun 2026) call the rationale had been restated in capital-allocation language — 'sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery' — while the timeline slipped to an NCLT hearing in the first week of June and another 60–75 days, with management insisting its own compliances were 100% done and the delay was purely court process (summer vacation).

points.point: Management formally introduced the separation as a two-step composite scheme — RGML merging into RIL, then the Mobility Undertaking demerging into a separately listed Refex Mobility Limited — framed as unlocking focused value for stakeholders.
points.quote: On this note, I would like to briefly mention that the de-merger of Refex Green Mobility Limited from Refex Industries Limited is in progress through a composite scheme comprising two steps.

points.quote: Post-demerger, the mobility vertical will pursue its growth plan independently with strategic and financial flexibility.

points.point: On a question about ash and coal being over 96% of revenue and future segment margins, Anil Jain said mobility will stop being consolidated once listed, so RIL's reported mix becomes ash/coal plus wind (whose EBITDA margins he said are not very different).
points.quote: Like we said that we are demerging the mobility business so hopefully in the next few months it will be a separate listed entity and the results will not get consolidated after that.

points.point: The same focus logic was applied to power trading, which was wound up entirely on margin and strategic-fit grounds — evidence the demerger is part of a broader portfolio pruning.
points.quote: We have decided to wind this up completely because the margins in power trading were extremely low and this was not in alignment with what we were doing where our majority of focus was.

points.point: Opening remarks tied the separation to a wider capital-redeployment and return-profile agenda, announcing exits from power trading and refrigerant gases alongside the mobility demerger (Q3 PBT Rs.89 crores, up 24% QoQ; PAT Rs.67 crores, up 29% QoQ).
points.quote: In order to achieve stronger return profiles by redeploying capital and focus towards core businesses, the management has taken a strategic call to exit power trading and refrigerant gas business.

points.point: Answering Ananya Khanna of Alpha Alternatives on timeline and synergies, Anil Jain disclosed lenders as the gating item — final NOCs awaited before the scheme could be filed — and that mobility's debt travels with it; Dinesh Agarwal guided to April completion.
points.quote: Once it is demerged, the Refex Mobility will run as a separate entity where it will have more liberty to do its own business and also it will have its own, all the debt etc. will also move to that entity.

points.point: Pressed by individual investor Vivek Joshi on how assets split, Dinesh Agarwal quantified the transfer at Rs.220 crores of net assets and stressed RIL itself owns no RGML assets — it is a 100% subsidiary going to parallel separate listing.
points.quote: Okay. So from the net assets, Rs.220 Crores get transferred to Mobility, right?

points.point: Asked about the 3–5 year business mix, Anil Jain said standalone RIL becomes almost purely ash and coal handling, with mobility entirely out of consolidation and wind the other consolidated growth leg.
points.quote: Officially, on a standalone basis, Refex industries will have 100% business, maybe 95% business from ash and coal handling only.

points.point: Management restated the rationale in capital-allocation terms and said key regulatory and procedural milestones were already achieved, with the process on track for operational separation.
points.quote: We believe this structure will create sharper operational focus, clear capital allocation and stronger long-term value discovery for all the stakeholders.

points.point: Mobility was presented as standalone-viable: INR100 crores+ revenue in three years, improving utilization and operating efficiency, moving toward profitability — supporting the case for an independent listing.
points.quote: Operationally, the mobility business continues to witness strong growth momentum and has crossed INR100 crores revenue this year with just 3 years of operation.

points.point: Asked by Vidyashankar R whether the demerger was stuck at NCLT or blocked by something else, Dinesh Agarwal said there is no challenge, only court process — hearing expected first week of June, completion in another 60–75 days, with all company-side compliances done.
points.quote: if we put a time line, another 60 to 75 days, this should get completed.

points.point: On funding the separation and renewables scale-up, the CFO said refinancing was done in the quarter to lower borrowing cost (with temporary processing charges) at both Venwind and RIL, and that capital is not a constraint.
points.quote: We have sufficient internal accrual and also the bank balance to fund the current and the future capital requirements.

points.point: The filing's core argument is dissimilarity of the two businesses on risk, competition, financial profile and return ratios — the structural reason they should not share one balance sheet or one equity story.
points.quote: The nature of risk and competition, financial profiles and return ratios involved in the Ash & Coal handling business of RIL are distinct from Green Mobility Business presently undertaken through its wholly owned subsidiary RGML.

points.point: The filing names the constituencies asking for separation — a different investor, lender and strategic-partner set for green mobility — as the reason to list it parallel to RIL rather than keep it as a subsidiary.
points.quote: The Green Mobility Business is capable of attracting a different set of investors, lenders, strategic partners and other stakeholders and have significant potential for growth and profitability.

points.point: Listed benefits include creating an independent global-scale mobility company, greater management focus in each business, independent collaboration, and letting investors choose exposure by risk profile.
points.quote: Creation of an independent global scale company focusing exclusively on Green Mobility Business Undertaking and taking advantage of the growth potential in the said respective sector;

points.point: The financing motive is explicit: separate, sharper access to both debt and equity markets as the mechanism for unlocking mobility's value; the scheme also asserts no added burden or prejudice to shareholders or creditors.
points.quote: Enabling focused and sharper capital market access (debt and equity) and thereby unlocking the value of the Green Mobility Business Undertaking and creating enhanced value for shareholders.

verdict.what_management_expects: RIL becomes a near-pure ash & coal handler — 95–100% of standalone revenue — with capital redeployed from exited power trading and refrigerant gas into core. RML lists in parallel with mirror shareholding, taking ~Rs.220 crores net assets and its own debt, free to raise its own capital and scale fleet toward profitability. Management expects sharper focus, clear capital allocation, value discovery.
verdict.gaps: No mobility valuation, EBITDA, debt quantum or record/listing date; no reason lender NOCs lagged; no explanation why wind stays with RIL or mobility's standalone funding needs.

verdict.rationale: Management presents the split as a deliberate strategic step, not housekeeping: on 14 February 2026 the Boards of Religare Enterprises (REL) and Religare Finvest (RFL) approved demerging the group's financial services businesses from its insurance business into two focused, independently listed entities, with REL's lending, broking and ancillary support services moving into RFL on a going-concern basis while the investment in Care Health Insurance stays in REL, leaving REL a pure-play health insurance holding company; REL shareholders get 1 RFL share for every 1 REL share, and RFL (today unlisted, an RBI middle-layer NBFC) is to list in Q1 FY2028. The stated rationale rests on four pillars: (1) streamlined business focus and a simplified structure, giving each side its own business model, growth strategy, capital deployment and performance metrics; (2) unlocking shareholder value through RFL's separate listing, which management says will enhance investor participation, facilitate targeted capital raising for the lending/broking business and allow more efficient allocation of management resources; (3) focused management attention and talent alignment, with dedicated leadership teams per entity so decision-making becomes faster, execution more focused and market response nimbler — explicitly tied to the senior hires under way (Group General Counsel Babu Rao from Bajaj Finance, Group CHRO Indranil Choudhury from UTI Mutual Fund, plus business leaders being identified); and (4) enhanced risk management and compliance, with risk policies and internal compliance frameworks tailored to each segment rather than one blended set. The enabling trigger management cites is the change of control — 'the takeover of REL by Burman Gr[oup]' — alongside strong promoter commitment: subscription to 50% of the preferential/rights issue with an INR750 crore commitment, open-market buying lifting promoter holding to ~30.3% (29.75% fully diluted on warrant conversion against 70.25% public), and an INR1,500 crore raise at REL level earmarked INR600 crore to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking and ~INR375 crore for general corporate purposes. The problem being solved is a holding company in which an insurer and a cleaned-up but sub-scale lending/broking stack sat together, confusing shareholders, diluting management focus and blocking segment-specific capital raising — against a backdrop of loss-making units (a subsidiary at an INR8.87 crore H1 FY26 loss versus INR6.63 crore in H1 FY25, and an INR5.93 crore loss in Q3 FY26 on revenue of INR7.11 crore versus INR7.79 crore) and badly under-levered lenders (NBFC net worth ~INR800 crore, HFC ~INR200 crore in Nov 2025; RFL later cited at INR900–1,000 crore net worth with ~INR600 crore cash and needing no fresh capital). Management also ties the demerger directly to scale ambitions: 'Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.' Mechanically it is a scheme of arrangement under Sections 230–232 of the Companies Act 2013 needing regulatory, shareholder and creditor approvals, expected to run 15–18 months from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY28, with no change to REL's or RFL's existing regulatory registrations and, management insists, no operational disruption, no customer impact and no break in employee continuity.
verdict.evolution: On the Nov 2025 call the only demerger actually done was a small one — Religare Broking's e-governance business (a ~56,500-strong distributed-agent network for PAN/TAN/eTDS and bill-payment services) moved into wholly-owned Religare Digital Solutions under an NCLT-approved scheme — while investors did the pushing: Vikas Shrivastav asked what the corporate structure would look like in two years and specifically about 'the demerger of Care and the other two, three subsidiaries from the HoldCo', and Dixit Doshi asked whether value unlocking would come via a Care Health IPO or a demerger; management answered only with leadership hiring and the cleaning up of RFL's legacy issues. By the Feb 2026 call the plan was formal — boards approved it on 14 Feb 2026, and management laid out the four-pillar rationale, the 1:1 share entitlement, the retention of Care in REL and the 15–18 month path to a Q1 FY28 RFL listing. On the May 13, 2026 call the structure was unchanged but shareholder attention had moved past it: Sarvesh Gupta (Maximal Capital) and Vikas Srivastava (RBC) pressed on the holding company discount created by Care remaining a subsidiary of a listed REL and on a reverse merger of Care (noting the 19%-to-26% look-through gap and creeping-acquisition limits), with Arjun Lamba saying Kedaara remains a committed long-term partner, that separating FS from insurance was 'number one', and that the reverse-merger idea would be evaluated and answered later. By the time of the NSE observation letter (July 7, 2026) the scheme had cleared exchange no-objection under Regulation 37 and moved toward NCLT filing.

points.point: The only separation completed at this point was a sub-level one: Religare Broking's e-governance business (PAN/TAN/eTDS, digital and citizenship services, bill payments, run through ~56,500 distributed agents) was carved into wholly-owned Religare Digital Solutions under an NCLT-approved scheme.
points.quote: I am happy to share that during the quarter, e -governance business of Religare Broking has been demerged and transferred to Religare Digital Solutions Limited which is a wholly -owned subsidiary of Religare Broking Limited, pursuant to the scheme of arrangement approved by the Honorable NCLT.

points.point: An investor, not management, first raised separating Care and other subsidiaries out of the HoldCo, asking what the corporate structure would look like two years out; management had no structural answer and replied on leadership hiring instead.
points.quote: Specific question I am asking is r egarding the demerger of Care and the other two, three subsidiaries from the HoldCo and in terms of any plans, what are the plans there?

points.point: A second investor framed the choice explicitly as IPO versus demerger as the route to unlocking value in Care Health, showing the value-unlock question was shareholder-driven before the scheme existed.
points.quote: And in terms of your initial comments on the value unlocking, if you can j ust touch upon whether we will be looking for an IPO for the care health business or we will be better off with the de -merger of the business?

points.point: Management described the lenders as cleaned up but massively under-levered and un-capitalised — NBFC net worth around INR800 crore and the HFC around INR200 crore, with no equity infused into either — which is the capital-deployment problem the later separate listing is meant to address.
points.quote: And they continue to have that kind of a net worth because we have not infused any equity in these two businesses so far.

points.point: Management introduced the board-approved demerger of the financial services and insurance businesses into two focused listed entities as a strategic imperative aimed at value unlock, business clarity and long-term growth, with the Burman Group takeover of REL cited as the first converging enabling factor.
points.quote: It is a strategic imperati ve step designed to unlock shareholder value, create business clarity and position the resulting entities for sustained long - term growth.

points.point: Pillar one: separating financial services from insurance so each entity has its own business model, growth strategy, capital deployment and performance metrics instead of a blended holding-company profile.
points.quote: The segregation of financial services from insurance business is to create a focused entity with specific business model, growth strategy, capital deployment and performance metrics for t he teams.

points.point: Pillar two: RFL's independent listing is expected to unlock value, widen investor participation, enable targeted capital raising for the lending/broking business and allow more efficient allocation of management resources.
points.quote: It will facilitate targeted capital raising for this business and enable more efficient allocation of management resources, thereby supporting sustainable growth and long -term value creation by this newly created company.

points.point: Pillars three and four: dedicated leadership teams per entity to make decision-making faster and market response nimbler (and to give clear mandates to the senior leaders being hired), plus risk and compliance frameworks tailored to each segment.
points.quote: The demerger enables implementation of spec ific risk management policies and internal compliance frameworks tailored to ea

points.point: Mechanics: REL's lending, broking and ancillary support services go to RFL on a going-concern basis with Care retained in REL; RFL issues shares 1:1 to REL shareholders and then lists, with Religare Broking as its direct subsidiary and Religare Housing Finance as a fellow subsidiary in affordable housing.
points.quote: The lending, broking and ancillary support services held under REL shall be demer ged into RFL on a going concern basis. The investment in CARE shall continue to be retained in REL.

points.point: Process and timeline: a Sections 230–232 scheme requiring regulatory, shareholder and creditor approvals, taking 15–18 months to a Q1 FY28 completion, with no change to existing regulatory registrations and no disruption to operations, customers or employees.
points.quote: The company expects the entire process to take 15 to 18 months starting from the current quarter and shall culminate in the first quarter of FY ‘28.

points.point: Management restated the end-state — RFL as an integrated financial services platform, REL as a pure-play health insurance holding company via Care — alongside promoter commitment of INR750 crore (50% of the preferential/rights issue) and a stake lifted to ~30.3% through open-market purchases.
points.quote: Under the proposed demerger, REL's lending, broking and ancillary financial services business will move to RFL, while REL will become a pure play health insurance holding company through its stake in Care Health Insurance business.

points.point: Shareholders pushed back that the chosen structure leaves Care as a subsidiary of a listed REL and therefore creates a holding company discount, repeating a concern first raised on the prior call and asking for a reverse merger of Care.
points.quote: So I think in the last call also, there were concerns raised regarding this demerger process and the hold ing company discount, which can be created because of this sort of a structure.

points.point: Arjun Lamba, for the promoters, acknowledged the investor concern but ranked clean separation of FS from insurance as the first priority, saying the reverse-merger question would be evaluated at an appropriate stage given how complex and regulator-dependent such restructurings are.
points.quote: And for us, number one has been to separate the FS business from the insurance business and to provide a clean structure so that the shareholders can understand, th e management can be very focused in doing what they have to do.

points.point: The separation is tied to a capital plan: of INR1,500 crore raised at REL, INR600 crore goes to Care, INR250 crore to housing finance, INR200 crore to broking and ~INR375 crore to general corporate purposes, while RFL (INR900–1,000 crore net worth, ~INR600 crore cash) needs none — all in service of scaling each business.
points.quote: Our intent is to scale all of these business to make them meaningful and sizable and part of this demerger is on account of this.

points.point: The filing text supplied is NSE's July 7, 2026 Regulation 37 observation letter, not a rationale narrative: it conveys 'No objection' to filing the scheme with NCLT and requires REL to disclose the need for and rationale of the demerger, synergies, valuation and swap-ratio basis, segment financials, risks and RBI approvals to shareholders — i.e. the substantive rationale is still owed to shareholders, not stated here.
points.quote:
Need for demerger, rationale of the scheme, synergies of  business of the entities involved in 
the scheme, impact of the scheme on the shareholders and cost benefit analysis of the s cheme.

points.point: Listing of RFL is conditional, not automatic — it is at the Exchange's discretion and subject to SEBI approval, an Information Memorandum, newspaper advertisement, frozen shares until trading permission, no change in RFL's shareholding or control between record date and listing, and trading starting within 60 days of the NCLT order.
points.quote:
However, the listing of shares of Religare Finvest Limited  
is at the discretion of the Exchange.

verdict.what_management_expects: RFL: an integrated, independently listed financial services platform with its own leadership, risk framework, targeted capital raising and faster decisions, scaling an under-levered NBFC (INR900–1,000 crore net worth, ~INR600 crore cash), housing finance and broking. REL: a pure-play health insurance holdco around Care, growing 24%-plus with INR600 crore infusion. Both: unlocked shareholder value, clearer structure, wider investor participation, no operational or employee disruption.
verdict.gaps: No swap-ratio or valuation basis, no fix for the Care holding-company discount or reverse merger, truncated Burman-takeover driver, no demerged-segment financials, RBI approval detail, or cost-benefit numbers.

verdict.rationale: Maharashtra Seamless Limited (MSL) is splitting into three listed entities: a composite scheme approved by the Board on 07 October 2026 (appointed date 01 October 2026) demerges Demerged Undertaking 1 into MSL Seamless Tubes Limited (MSTL) and Demerged Undertaking 2 into United Seamless Limited (USL), both currently wholly owned subsidiaries whose ₹1,00,000-share pre-scheme capital is cancelled and reissued to MSL shareholders. On FY2025-26 operational turnover, DU1 is ₹793 crore (16.98%), DU2 ₹693 crore (14.84%) and the remainder staying with MSL ₹3,185 crore (68.18%) of ₹4,671 crore total. The Board's stated reason is that MSL runs multiple undertakings with distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies, customer bases, logistics, capital requirements and growth trajectories — specifically three manufacturing plants on three different technology platforms (CPE at Nagothane, MPM at Mangaon, FQM at Telangana) serving different industry segments, plus a drilling/rig business and renewable power assets. The scheme says manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have different capital intensity and funding needs, so separation permits better assessment of capital needs, focused deployment and flexibility for expansion; renewable assets move with the undertaking they power, for energy-management efficiency and sustainability support. The rig business is called out as having distinct operational and commercial characteristics versus pipe manufacturing, warranting focused management and operational planning. The Board also expects improved transparency through independent financial and operational reporting, better performance evaluation and long-term value creation. It is structured to be value-neutral — 1 share of each resulting company (INR 5) for every 5 MSL shares (INR 5), keeping the same proportionate holding (promoters 70.3008%, public 29.6992%), with no cash consideration, no creditor compromise and listing of MSTL and USL on BSE and NSE. The trigger on the calls was investor pressure on what MSL would do with the rig and its surplus cash.
verdict.evolution: The idea first surfaces on the Nov 2023 call as a rig disposal, not a demerger: analyst Vikash Singh asks whether the plan to sell the single rig has been dropped given strong oil prices and cash flows, and D.P. Jindal says it has not been dropped but they are 'looking for the right time to hive off', adding they already have a plan for ₹852 crore of cash and want investors to benefit from it. By the Nov 2024 call the option set has widened and acquired a date — analyst Rishabh describes it as a plan to 'demerge or sell' the rig business post May 2025 — but Kaushal Bengani declines to give any realisation expectation because the matter had not yet reached the Board. By the scheme filing of 07 October 2026 the plan has changed shape entirely: no sale, and far wider scope than the rig — a two-way demerger of whole operational undertakings (manufacturing plants on different technology platforms, drilling and renewable power assets) into two separately listed companies, with the rig segregation now only one of seven stated benefits.

points.point: An analyst asks whether the long-stated plan to sell MSL's single rig has been abandoned given good oil prices and strong free cash flow; the Chairman says the plan stands but is waiting on timing.
points.quote: No, we have not dropped, but we are looking for the right time to hive off.

points.point: Pressed on what MSL would do with surplus cash it has no avenues to deploy, D.P. Jindal cites an existing plan for ₹852 crore, openness to opportunities in the same line of business, and a commitment that investors benefit from the cash.
points.quote: First, we have a plan for these 852 crores, and then we are also open for any new opportunity in the same field of business.

points.point: An analyst frames the rig plan as demerger-or-sale with a post-May 2025 timeline, asking what realisation and how long the process takes — showing the demerger route was already in investors' understanding two years before the scheme.
points.quote: Also on the rig business that you have, I understand that you are planning to demerge or sell it post May '25.

points.point: Kaushal Bengani refuses any valuation or realisation figure, saying the rig separation is an intention not yet taken to the Board, and that communication will follow Board approval.
points.quote: We don't have an expectation figure right now because that matter has not yet been discussed at Board level.

points.point: Capex discussion is confined to the ongoing Telangana debottlenecking and what is already in the presentation; no restructuring or separate-capital-pool argument is offered on the call.
points.quote: We have that. That is why we are doing the debottlenecking at Telangana.

points.point: The Board's threshold finding is that MSL houses several undertakings that differ on nearly every operating dimension, justifying reorganisation into separate focused companies with identical proportionate shareholding.
points.quote: The said undertakings having distinct geographies, product profiles, technologies used, operational requirements, customer profile and base, market focus, logistics consideration, commercial considerations and growth opportunities.

points.point: Benefit (a): the three manufacturing sites — Nagothane, Mangaon and Telangana — serve different industry segments and are to become independent verticals with dedicated management.
points.quote: The manufacturing undertakings at Nagothane, Mangaon and Telangana cater to different industry segments and operate with distinct product portfolios, customer profiles and market dynamics.

points.point: Benefit (b): the plants run three different pipe-making technologies, each needing its own specialised management, modernisation path and technical expertise.
points.quote: The manufacturing facilities operate on different technological platforms, including CPE technology at Nagothane, MPM technology at Mangaon and FQM technology at Telangana, each requiring specialized operational management, modernization initiatives and technical expertise.

points.point: Benefit (d) — the capital-allocation argument: pipe manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy have unlike capital intensity and funding profiles, so separation sharpens assessment of capital needs and expansion flexibility.
points.quote: The manufacturing, drilling and renewable energy businesses have different capital intensity and funding requirements.

points.point: Benefit (e): renewable power assets are not pooled centrally but ride along with the undertaking they serve, for energy-management efficiency and sustainability support.
points.quote: The renewable power assets proposed to be transferred along with the respective undertakings are expected to provide better operational alignment, energy management efficiencies and support sustainability initiatives of the corresponding businesses.

points.point: Benefit (f) carries forward the rig question raised on both calls, now as segregation rather than sale, justified by the rig business being commercially unlike pipe making.
points.quote: The rig business has distinct operational and commercial characteristics as compared to the pipe manufacturing business.

points.point: Benefit (g): independent reporting for each entity is expected to improve transparency and performance evaluation and create long-term value — the closest the filing comes to a valuation-rerating argument.
points.quote: The proposed demerger would result in creation of focused business entities with independent financial and operational reporting, thereby enhancing transparency, improving performance evaluation and facilitating long-term value creation for stakeholders.

points.point: Scale of what leaves MSL: DU1 ₹793 crore (16.98%) and DU2 ₹693 crore (14.84%) of FY2025-26 operational turnover, against ₹3,185 crore (68.18%) retained, on a ₹4,671 crore total.
points.quote: Demerged Undertaking 1 793 16.98% Demerged Undertaking 2 693 14.84% Remaining 3185 68.18% Total 4671 100.00%

points.point: Consideration is paper, not cash: a 1-for-5 share entitlement in each resulting company, expressly engineered to leave shareholder economics unchanged (promoters 70.3008%, public 29.6992% in both MSTL and USL).
points.quote: The above share exchange ratios shall ensure same proportionate shareholding structure of Resulting Company 1 and Resulting Company 2 with Demerged Company and hence Scheme shall be value neutral to the Demerged Company's shareholders.

points.point: Both resulting companies are to be listed, making this a three-way listed split rather than an internal reorganisation; creditors are untouched, with no compromise offered and liabilities following their undertakings.
points.quote: The equity shares of MSTL and USL shall be listed and admitted to trading on BSE and NSE pursuant to the Scheme subject to receipt of requisite approvals from statutory and regulatory authorities.

verdict.what_management_expects: Three focused, separately listed entities: each undertaking pursuing an independent growth strategy with dedicated management, technology-specific operational focus and strategies tailored to its end-user sectors; operational efficiencies and optimum resource utilisation; better assessment of capital needs, focused deployment and expansion flexibility across manufacturing, drilling and renewables; renewable assets aligned to the businesses they power; independent reporting improving transparency, performance evaluation and long-term stakeholder value. Value-neutral to shareholders.
verdict.gaps: No margin, EBITDA, valuation or rerating figures; no asset-to-undertaking mapping; no mention of lenders, partners, investor demands for demerger, timelines, costs, or why sale became demerger.

verdict.rationale: No earnings-call passages were supplied with this request — the "CALL PASSAGES" section is empty — so everything below comes solely from the Regulation 30 filings dated 1st October, 2026 and the scheme rationale section. The transaction is not a spin-off of a business out of the listed company but the reverse: a demerger of the "Sunteck City 4th Avenue Undertaking", a residential real estate project, out of Satguru Corporate Services Private Limited (the Demerged Company, a wholly owned subsidiary) and into Sunteck Realty Limited (the Resulting Company, the listed entity), on a going concern basis under Sections 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013. Management characterises it twice in the filing as "essentially an internal reorganisation between Sunteck and its wholly owned subsidiary - Satguru." The stated benefits are three: consolidation of the Demerged Business Undertaking; achieving administrative and operational efficiencies; and efficient pooling and deployment of financial and managerial resources so as to "facilitate project-specific capital allocation and funding strategies." The only quantification given is scale: the Demerged Business Undertaking's turnover for the year ended 31 March 2026 was Rs. ~869 Crs, representing ~77% of Sunteck's total consolidated turnover for FY ended 31st March 2026 — i.e. the group's dominant revenue stream currently sits one level below the listed entity, which is the structural anomaly the scheme removes. Because Satguru is wholly owned, no shares are issued, there is no cash consideration and no share exchange ratio, there is no change in the shareholding patterns of either company, and no fresh listing is required since Sunteck's equity shares are already listed on the Stock Exchanges. The scheme remains subject to requisite statutory and regulatory approvals including the approval of the National Company Law Tribunal. The same board meeting (6.45 p.m. to 7.05 p.m. on Thursday, 1st October, 2026) also approved, on the Audit Committee's recommendation, the appointment of Ernst & Young LLP as Internal Auditor up to 31st March, 2027.
verdict.evolution: No call-by-call evolution can be reconstructed: no earnings-call passages were provided, so there is no dated record of how or when the idea surfaced or changed. The only dated evidence is 1st October, 2026, when the Board of Directors approved the Scheme of Arrangement and the company disclosed it to NSE (Symbol: SUNTECK) and BSE (Scrip Code: 512179) under Regulation 30 read with the SEBI Master Circular dated 30th January, 2026. The filing presents the rationale as settled and final, with no reference to prior discussion, to investor, lender or partner requests, or to any earlier version of the plan.

verdict.rationale: Management frames the separation as two linked moves to unwind a conglomerate structure in which crop protection and seeds compete for the same capital. On the Feb 2, 2026 call, Toshan Tamhane gave three objectives for the Advanta (seeds) IPO: (a) deleveraging of UPL Ltd's balance sheet, (b) value unlock for KKR, which put in a cheque of '$300-plus million' into Advanta more than three years earlier, and (c) the argument that 'the needs of crop protection in terms of the cash flows, capital allocation are very different from that of the seeds business,' citing Corteva's own announced split of crop protection and seeds as validation, and describing Advanta as the eighth largest seeds player globally with 'a journey and destiny of its own.' Bikash Prasad stressed the Advanta listing is an offer for sale, not a primary raise — Advanta is cash-surplus and does not need the money — with proceeds going to the group 'largely for deleveraging of the group balance sheet,' and valuation to be set by a book-building price discovery process under applicable law. The separately filed Scheme (board-approved February 20, 2026) then consolidates the India crop protection business held in UPL SAS (UPL holds 90.91%) and the international crop protection business held via UPL Corp / UPL Cayman (UPL holds 77.78%) into UPL Global ('UPL 2'), to be listed — billed as the 'World's Second Largest Listed Pure-Play Crop Protection Platform' — via amalgamation of UPL SAS into UPL, a vertical demerger of India crop protection into UPL Global, and amalgamation of UPL Corp into UPL Global, with no cash consideration. The stated problems it solves: a complicated group structure with misaligned shareholder interests across layered subsidiaries, blurred value discovery for investors, constrained independent capital-raising, and split managerial and board focus; the demerged India crop protection undertaking was INR 24,120 Mn of turnover in FY25, 31.15% of combined UPL 1 turnover. Ratios: 1,000 UPL 1 shares (INR 2) for every 48 UPL SAS shares (INR 10); 1,000 UPL 2 shares for every 213 UPL Cayman shares (USD 1); and 1:1 UPL 2 for UPL 1 on the demerger, leaving UPL 1 promoters at 33.09% (from 33.51%) and UPL 2 at 71.56% promoter / 28.44% public. On the call an analyst (Tarang) pushed back hard that deleveraging and an exit for an external shareholder make sense but value creation for a UPL minority shareholder does not, given how the entities are stacked — a challenge management did not rebut.
verdict.evolution: The passages supplied are all tagged [Feb 2026], so the three-year arc is not visible in them; within that window the sequence is a Q3 FY26 earnings call where the Advanta seeds IPO was raised only in Q&A, under analyst questioning, and was defended as an offer for sale for group deleveraging plus a KKR exit, with the crop-protection-versus-seeds capital allocation logic offered last ('And lastly, third...'). Management there pointed outward to Corteva's announced crop protection/seeds split rather than to a UPL plan of its own, and declined to discuss Advanta's valuation beyond saying the Board would assess market conditions at the time. Weeks later, on February 20, 2026, the Board formalised the far larger step in a composite scheme of arrangement creating a separately listed pure-play crop protection entity (UPL Global), where the rationale shifts from deleveraging and partner exit to structural simplification, clearer value discovery and independent capital raising. So the idea moves from a cash-raising/partner-exit transaction at the seeds subsidiary to a full two-listed-entity reorganisation of the parent.

verdict.rationale: Management says SKF India is demerging its Industrial business into a new entity, SKF India (Industrial) Limited, leaving Automotive in the listed SKF India Limited, not to fix a problem but because the two businesses have diverged: 'external' drivers differ (Industrial is driven by infrastructure spend and China Plus One; Automotive by EVs and CAFE norms), customer needs differ (Industrial serves many verticals such as steel, heavy, metals, railways, wind; Automotive serves a few large OEMs plus aftermarket), and manufacturing philosophy differs (one needs large-batch processing, the other shorter cycle times, smaller batches and more innovative products). The stated purpose is 'two fit-for-purpose independent companies' that can each accelerate growth and profitability, with independent management focus (separate board, leadership, sales and manufacturing teams), tailored innovation, tailored capital deployment, higher manufacturing efficiency, more agility, and better standalone visibility for investors. Management repeatedly stressed the split is not driven by weakness: FY25 revenue was about Rs 5,000 crore with 17.2% EBITDA, 11.5% PBT, ROCE 28%-29% and ROE 21%-22%, and a five-year CAGR of 16.4% in revenue, 17.4% in PBT and 17.5% in EPS. On economics, carve-out financials submitted to SEBI showed FY23-24 margins of roughly 14%-15% for both sides, similar despite very different mixes because Automotive is 95% localized while Industrial is only about 40% localized and carries more traded product; management expects Industrial margins to normalize upward as localization rises (overall over 80% of components now sourced locally, with a further ~5 percentage point gain targeted in 3-4 years). The split also reclassifies the tractor business (agriculture and electricals), today reported under Automotive, into Industrial, which is why the scheme shows Industrial at 63% of FY24 revenue versus the ~50%-54% quoted in quarterly commentary. Asset allocation was disclosed progressively: Haridwar 100% Automotive (4 lines), Bangalore 7 of 10 lines and ~85% of land to Automotive, Pune 12 of 22 lines Automotive and 10 Industrial with land split 52:48 and a new Industrial factory to be built next to the existing Automotive plant, and manpower 55%-60% Automotive versus 40%-45% Industrial. Costs of the split are real and visible: Q1 FY26 margins fell 530 basis points, partly from one-time demerger IT and consultant costs that management said will continue for the next year to year and a half.
verdict.evolution: By the Feb 13, 2025 Q3 FY25 call the scheme was already filed with the exchanges and three years of carve-out financials were with SEBI, so the discussion was defensive and definitional - reconciling 63% versus 54% Industrial revenue, auto-versus-industrial margins and localization - with investors (Mukesh Saraf, Viraj Kacharia, Ravi Purohit) pressing for pro forma segment numbers ahead of a shareholder vote. Management then held a dedicated Demerger Update Call on April 09, 2025 devoted to rationale, pro forma financials and timeline, and the May 19, 2025 Q4 call formalized the 'two fit-for-purpose independent companies' language and first disclosed the plant-level split (Haridwar to Automotive, Bangalore 80%-85% Automotive, Pune split with a new Industrial factory). The June 30, 2025 investor meet went deeper: it named the external drivers (infrastructure and China Plus One versus EVs and CAFE norms), gave the first forward split guidance (Automotive 10%-12%, Industrial 8%-10% growth to FY28, Industrial faster thereafter, 17%-19% EBITDA maintained), and confirmed separate boards and leadership before the effective date. By the Aug 07, 2025 Q1 FY26 call the rationale was unchanged but execution detail and cost arrived - line-by-line, land and manpower splits, shareholder approval obtained July 14, 2025, NCLT decision expected September - and the scheme documents then record the NSE observation letter of March 28, 2025, the NCLT filing of April 09, 2025, the October 15, 2025 record date and the October 17, 2025 allotment of 4,94,37,963 shares.

points.quote: I would say this gives us the opportunity to actually innovate more and add more products specific to the industries we want to serve

Will it be possible for you to kind of give us at least 2-year or a 3-year pro forma numbers between industrial and automotive, just to get -- see because the thing is it's a big event that is happening and it will be useful if shareholders have all the information before.

points.quote: The purpose of today's call is to provide a comprehensive update on the demerger process, its strategic rationale, expected benefits and next steps.

points.point: Vasudevan said keeping investors informed on the logic of segregating Automotive from Industrial was itself a priority of the exercise.

points.point: The core stated reason: two fit-for-purpose independent companies to accelerate growth and profitability, because the businesses have different macros, customer needs and manufacturing focus.
points.quote: As you remember, the overall -- the reason for the demerger is we are creating 2 fit-for-purpose independent company, which will accelerate both growth and profitability in both companies.

points.point: Manufacturing philosophy is cited as a concrete operational conflict inside one company: large-batch production for one business versus short-cycle, small-batch, more innovative production for the other.
points.quote: The 2 entities will have different kind of manufacturing philosophy, 1 more batch processing, large batch processing; 1 more shorter cycle times, shorter cycles, smaller batches but more innovative products.

points.point: Benefits listed were independent management focus, better customer value proposition, segment-specific innovation, agility, manufacturing efficiency, tailored capital deployment and standalone investor visibility.
points.quote: Tailored capital deployment, which is very important also between the 2 SKF India Limited May 19, 2025 Page 5 of 14 entities; and finally, just more visibility for the -- our investors, all of you, to be able to see the performance of the 2 entities independently.

points.point: First plant-level disclosure: Haridwar fully to Automotive, Bangalore 80%-85% to Automotive, Pune split, with a brand-new Industrial factory to be built next to the existing Automotive plant at Pune.
points.quote: And Pune: So there will actually be a new factory setup for just industrial, next to the current automotive one.

points.point: Process status: filed with NCLT in Q2 CY25, with shareholder and creditor meetings to follow and listing targeted for Q4 CY25 or Q3 FY25-26.
points.quote: So broadly on track to finish the listing by Q4 calendar year of this year or Q3 calendar year 25-26, okay.

points.quote: Customer needs are also very different.

points.point: Forward split guidance: Automotive 10%-12% and Industrial 8%-10% growth near term, with Industrial faster beyond FY28 once the new plant is built and products are more localized, and 17%-19% EBITDA maintained.

verdict.what_management_expects: Two fit-for-purpose listed companies, each with its own board, leadership, sales and plants: Automotive to press e-mobility leadership, faster launches and capacity calls; Industrial to grow faster per vertical, build a new Pune plant and lift margins as localization rises from ~40%. verdict.rationale: The filing is not a classic value-unlocking spin-off: Thermax is pulling businesses INTO the listed parent and leaving only a residual activity outside. Two linked steps sit in one Scheme of Arrangement and Amalgamation. (1) Amalgamation: a wholly-owned subsidiary engaged in 'setting up Energy Projects, Energy Exchange Platform and providing Energy Services including provision of electrostatic precipitators, regenerative air preheaters and related services' — a shell-sized entity with Rs 10.0 cr paid-up capital, Rs 0.6 cr net worth and Rs 0.8 cr total income as on March 31, 2026 — is merged into Thermax Ltd. (net worth Rs 4,427.09 cr, total income Rs 6,518.2 cr) to 'simplify overall group structure and reduce administrative overheads,' with management claiming 'a significant improvement in certain key financial ratios,' annual group cost savings, and 'stronger financial stability and valuation metrics' that present 'a more accurate picture of the Company's financial strength.' (2) Demerger: the Technology/EPC undertaking of Thermax Bioenergy Solutions Private Limited (incorporated August 12, 2022; CIN U40107PN2022PTC213848; WOS), covering Engineering, Procurement and Construction scope for Bio-CNG projects, is carved out and transferred into Thermax Ltd. because it is 'in line with the business of the Company' — turnover Rs 239.35 cr, or 3.67% of Thermax's FY26 revenue. The stated problem it solves is focus and vertical segregation: once EPC leaves, Bioenergy Solutions is meant to concentrate on its remaining O&M segment, while each entity 'pursue[s] growth opportunities that are more aligned with their own industry dynamics.' Notably, Bioenergy Solutions carries negative net worth of Rs (106.9) cr against Rs 38.0 cr paid-up capital and Rs 260.9 cr total income, which the rationale text never addresses. Both steps are cashless and cosmetically neutral to owners: all transferor/demerged shares are already held by Thermax and its nominees, the transferor's shares 'stand cancelled,' no new shares are issued, and there is no change in the shareholding pattern; Bioenergy Solutions stays an unlisted wholly-owned subsidiary.
verdict.evolution: No earnings-call passages were supplied — the 'CALL PASSAGES:' section of the prompt was empty, so no call-by-call development of the idea can be traced and no call dates exist in the source. The only datable evidence is the scheme filing itself, dated against financials as on March 31, 2026, alongside unaudited standalone and consolidated results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. Within the filing, the sequencing is logical rather than chronological: Annexure A sets out the amalgamation of the energy-projects/energy-exchange subsidiary, and Annexure B the demerger of the Bio-CNG EPC undertaking into the same listed entity.
