verdict.rationale: Management frames the demerger as a strategic refocusing: Piccadily wants to be a global alco-bev company, so on the April 29, 2026 call (tagged May 2026) it announced that, with management and Board approval granted the prior day, it had filed a scheme of demerger of the sugar business into a new entity, with KPMG as advisor on the exercise and the scheme filed with SEBI; the next steps are SEBI go-ahead then NCLT, with completion envisaged by FY'27. The stated intent is to 'pool our human and capital resources just for the Alco-Bev business' and focus only on the Alco-Bev brand portfolio, while sugar — described as a 'traditional heritage business' — is separated and listed as its own entity rather than sold (management did not say sale was the plan when asked). The backdrop is an alco-bev business carrying the group: FY26 consolidated PBT up 79% from INR35 crores to INR63 crores on premiumisation (Indri, Cashmir Vodka), standalone revenue up 33% from INR270 crores to INR364 crores, standalone PBT up 17% to INR63 crores and PAT up 14% from INR40 crores to INR46 crores, with the distillery/Alco-Bev business growing 42% in FY26; FY27 is expected to be 'exceptional' at 60%–70% growth, helped by the Indri plant adding INR250–300 crores and the 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh greenfield adding INR300–400 crores, with 3x–4x revenue in 3–4 years and a Scotland malt distillery in the works (land, licences and approvals in place, construction starting). The scheme filing quantifies the demerged sugar division at 20.53% of the listed entity's FY26 turnover and sets a 1-for-9 share entitlement ratio (one PFEL share of INR10 for every nine PAIL shares of INR10), fixed on the sugar undertaking's turnover and assets, with no cash consideration and no change in PAIL's shareholding pattern. The filing's rationale is that separating the businesses lets each give 'focused attention for growth of their core businesses and attract required investments', brings greater business focus and shareholder value, unlocks value through price discovery of the individual entities, creates the right operating architecture with sharper individual strategies and 'clear capital allocation', and lets two separately listed companies attract their own specific investor sets and achieve financial flexibility. Resulting company Piccadily Food & Essentials Limited (PFEL) is currently a wholly owned subsidiary whose pre-scheme capital will be cancelled, and its new shares will be listed on BSE and NSE; the stock exchanges issued No Adverse Observation Letters dated August 14, 2026, intimated August 17, 2026.
verdict.evolution: The supplied material contains only one call — April 29, 2026 (tagged May 2026) — so the idea cannot be traced across the three years claimed; on that call management said only that 'we've been discussing this' before Board approval on April 28, 2026, giving no earlier dated discussion. Within that call it appears three times: first as a formal announcement of the filed scheme with SEBI/KPMG and an FY'27 completion target, then restated in the growth outlook as a demerger 'just to focus on the main Alco-Bev business', and finally in Q&A, where analyst Himanshu Shah asked whether the sugar business would be sold or separately listed and management clarified the intent is separate listing and pooling resources into Alco-Bev, not a sale. The only later step evidenced is procedural: BSE and NSE No Adverse Observation Letters dated August 14, 2026, intimated to the exchanges on August 17, 2026.

verdict.rationale: Pricol's board (approval announced June 27, 2026) is demerging its Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions ('DICVS') undertaking — driver information systems including connected, electronic, mechanical and electro-mechanical instrument clusters, integrated infotainment, advanced e-cockpit solutions, telematics, battery management systems and a few sensors — into Pricol Autotech Limited, leaving Pricol Limited with the Actuation, Control & Fluid Management Systems ('ACFMS') and Precision Products ('P3L') businesses. The scale cited is material: DICVS turnover of INR 2,424.63 crores for FY ending March 31, 2026, or 61.17% of consolidated turnover, with management stating both halves have 'acquired sufficient scale and maturity to function more effectively as focused standalone businesses.' The stated problem is that the two sides operate with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles inside one structure, which creates operational complexity, slow decision-making, and shared processes, policies, systems and governance that fit neither business. The fix is two focused platforms — an automotive technology entity and an automotive & industrial precision engineering entity — each with dedicated management, independent capital allocation, and its own governance, described as 'simpler, sharper and more agile' to meet fast-changing technology needs and dynamic market realities. Capital-markets reasoning is explicit: clearer visibility of each business's stakeholder value, growth prospects and investment merits, improved ability to attract strategic and financial investors, greater flexibility to access capital, and unlocking shareholder value. Mechanically it is value-neutral at the shareholder level — no cash consideration, 1:1 share entitlement (1 Pricol Autotech share of INR 1 face value per Pricol share), no change in Pricol's shareholding pattern, and Pricol Autotech's register mirroring Pricol's at 38.51% promoter / 61.49% public, with listing sought on NSE and BSE. Valuation rests on SSPA & Co's Share Entitlement Ratio Report dated 27th June 2026, with a fairness opinion from Saffron Capital Advisors.
verdict.evolution: No earnings call passages were supplied in this prompt — the 'CALL PASSAGES' section is empty, so the call-by-call emergence of the idea cannot be reconstructed from these texts. The only dated evidence here is the scheme filing itself: board approval of the scheme of arrangement announced Coimbatore, June 27th, 2026, with the share entitlement ratio report of the same date (27th June 2026). The filing's own framing — 'Over the years' the DICVS business 'has evolved into a differentiated platform,' and 'Over time with a well thoughtout and clear strategic intent' both businesses reached standalone scale — implies a multi-year build-up to the decision, but the filing does not date those earlier steps.

points.point: The demerged undertaking is the DICVS business, and the filing quantifies it as the majority of the group: INR 2,424.63 crores of turnover in FY ending March 31, 2026, equal to 61.17% of consolidated turnover.

points.point: Stated strategic motive: build a simpler, sharper, more agile entity able to keep pace with the technology cycle and market conditions specific to DICVS.
points.quote: The demerger of the DICVS Business is a strategic decision to create a simpler, sharper and more agile corporate entity, to meet the fast changing needs and technologies related to this business and its dynamic market realities.

points.point: The core problem named is mismatch inside one company — the two businesses differ on customers, competition, capital allocation and risk, and each has now reached standalone scale.
points.quote: The Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company currently operates with differing customer needs, competitive dynamics, capital allocation and risk profiles.

points.point: Both halves are said to have outgrown the combined structure, which is the filing's justification for separating now rather than earlier.
points.quote: Over time with a well thoughtout and clear strategic intent, both the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company have acquired sufficient scale and maturity to function more effectively as focused standalone businesses .

points.point: Benefit list includes independent capital allocation and faster decision-making via reduced complexity, plus dedicated management teams for each business.
points.quote: Financial flexibility for each entity to pursue investment decisions aligned with their respective business portfolios and market requirements ;

points.point: Explicit investor-facing rationale: separate platforms should make each business's value and growth visible and make it easier to attract strategic and financial investors and access capital.
points.quote: Creation of focused and independent business platforms for the Demerged Undertaking and the Remaining Business of the Demerged Company, with clear and enhanced visibility of their respective stakeholder value, growth prospects and investment merits, improved abilit y to attract strategic and financial investors to meet the needs of the respective business, greater flexibility to access capital, pursue growth and technology opportunities and implement their respective long -term strategies .

points.point: The structure created is two named platforms — an automotive technology entity (Pricol Autotech, DICVS) and an automotive & industrial precision engineering entity (Pricol Limited, holding ACFMS and P3L).
points.quote: Strategic demerger to create two focused  business platform s – an Automotive Technology Entity and an Automotive  & Industrial  Precision Engineering Entity, for a simpler, sharper and more agile structure meeting the fast -changing technological needs and the dynamic market realities

points.point: DICVS is characterised as having evolved into a differentiated platform needing its own long-term strategy, technology capabilities and partnerships for integrated solutions.
points.quote: The proposed demerger  recognises this evolution and enables the business to pursue independent long -term strategies, strengthen technology capabilities , partnerships for integrated solution offerings  and respond more effectively to changing industry dynamics.

points.point: Retained-business case: ACFMS is backed by growing domestic and export footprints in fluid management and control, and P3L is positioned for expanding precision components demand.
points.quote: The ACFMS and P3L businesses will continue to remain part of Pricol  Limited, with the ACFMS business being supported by growing domestic and export footprint s and opportunities in fluid management and control  solutions , and the P3L business being strategically positioned to capitali se on the expanding opportunity in precision  components.

points.point: Consideration is a value-neutral mirror split: no cash, 1:1 entitlement, Pricol Autotech's shareholding mirroring Pricol's (promoters 38.51%, public 61.49% post-scheme), with listing sought on NSE and BSE.
points.quote: Shareholders of Pricol Limited will receive one fully paid -up equity share of Pricol Autotech Limited for every one fully paid -up equity share held in Pricol Limited (1:1 share entitlement ratio) , resulting in the shareholding of Pricol Autotech Limited mirroring the shareholding of Pricol Limited , subject to the Scheme becoming effective.

verdict.what_management_expects: Pricol Autotech (DICVS): independent strategy, stronger technology capability and integrated-solution partnerships, dedicated leadership. Pricol (ACFMS + P3L): growth from domestic/export fluid management, control and precision components. For both: dedicated management, independent capital allocation, financial flexibility, lower complexity and faster decisions, tailored governance, better visibility of value and growth, easier access to strategic and financial investors and capital, unlocking shareholder value. No margin or return numbers given.

verdict.rationale: The separation management actually explains on these calls is the carve-out and demerger of the Softgel business and Stelis Biopharma (biologics/CDMO) into OneSource Specialty Pharma, announced in the quarter ended Sept 2023 and valued, as the analyst's number was confirmed by Arun Kumar, at around 17x FY24 EBITDA for both softgel and Steriscience. The stated purpose was to combine a very high-margin soft gelatin business with the biologics/drug-device platform to create a 'unique specialty CDMO platform' with a large GLP-1-led contract manufacturing order book (about 15 customers; patents partially off in FY25, main patents only in 2030, so revenue was development/R&D income today and commercial later), and to let Strides shareholders 'participate in value discovery' by holding 44% of OneSource (61% total public shareholding across the three companies). The second, equally explicit driver was balance-sheet repair: against roughly INR3,000 crores of debt, management said the announcement 'solves for the debt to EBITDA ratio' because the combined EBITDA of the two demerged companies was about INR1,200 crores, and INR283 crores of debt moved with the demerger. Third, it ended Strides' contingent exposure to Stelis — corporate guarantees were cut by almost INR600 crores by Feb 2024, with Arun Kumar saying all guarantees 'will go off the book' once listed; by Jan 2025 all guarantees were fully released and by May 2025 the entire INR705 crores of guarantees to Stelis had been closed. Lenders were a direct constituency: all significant NOCs from lenders were obtained, and lenders were accepting because 'there will also be that much less loans in OneSource'; OneSource also gained the ability to raise up to $100 million at relisting, with a bridge facility only until then. Post-demerger the retained Strides business was restated from an April 1, 2024 appointed date and reframed as a focused, bottom-line-led generics business (12%-15% revenue CAGR but much faster EBITDA CAGR), with Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 18.2%, gross margins held at 58%-59%, ROCE 14.9% vs 9.7% comparable, net debt/EBITDA down to 1.9x, and a INR3,188 crores accounting gain on demerger; management quantified the shareholder outcome as INR78.8 billion distributed 'in the form of demerger and listing'. Note that the filing text supplied here is a different, later transaction — the demerger of Arco Lab's Life Sciences and Digital Innovation business into Pivot Path (appointed date April 10, 2025; NCLT Bengaluru approval May 18/20, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) — and these documents are procedural intimations that contain no rationale section at all.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaces as an already-announced carve-out in the Sept 25, 2023 call ([Oct 2023]), where valuation (~17x FY24 EBITDA), the 44%/61% shareholding slides and the debt-to-EBITDA fix are debated; the Oct 30, 2023 call ([Nov 2023]) fleshes out the industrial logic (GLP-1 drug-device order book, ~15 customers, patents opening 2025-2030). By the Feb 2024 call it is an execution story — exchange queries, NOCs from lenders, guarantees down INR600 crores, NCLT filing targeted that quarter — and in May 2024 SEBI approval arrives as 'the last step' before a 3-4 quarter court process plus ~60 days to list. The Jan 30, 2025 call ([Feb 2025]) reports it done: OneSource listed, appointed date April 1, 2024, financials restated, all guarantees released; May 2025 and July 2025 ([Aug 2025]) use it as the proof point (INR705 crores guarantees closed, INR78.8 billion distributed, OneSource stake retained as 'a great strategic outcome'), and by May 2026 the softgel exit is only a footnote to resetting the US aspiration to $375-$400 million for FY28.

points.point: Management confirmed the analyst's valuation framing: both the softgel business and Steriscience were being valued at about 17x FY24 EBITDA in the scheme.
points.quote: So the valuation for soft gel as well as the Steriscience is around 17x FY ‘24 EBITDA.

points.point: Arun Kumar insisted the structure was a full demerger-cum-merger, not a partial one, when asked why it was not a 100% merger.
points.quote: Well, from what I know, it's a clean 100% demerger, merger into the scheme.

points.point: The presentation's own rationale, read back by an analyst, was value discovery for Strides shareholders through a 44% holding in OneSource, with 61% being total public shareholding across the merging companies.
points.quote: In presentation, at one slide you wrote that Strides shareholders to participate in value discovery by holding 44% in OneSource.

points.point: Asked how INR3,000 crores of debt would be cut, Arun Kumar said the demerger itself fixes leverage because the two demerged businesses carry about INR1,200 crores of combined EBITDA.
points.quote: So firstly, the announcements we made today solves for the debt to EBITDA ratio, because you'll also appreciate that the combined EBITDA of the two companies are now INR1,200 crores

points.point: The industrial logic: OneSource was carved out to house the GLP-1/drug-device contract manufacturing order book with ~15 customers, where patents open partially in FY25 and mainly only in 2030, so near-term income is R&D and development batches.
points.quote: But having said that, we do get a lot of R&D income and we do hold a very large order book for our contract manufacturing opportunities led by GLP in OneSource which in a company that we just announced is a carve-out in the last quarter.

points.point: De-risking Strides was quantified: corporate guarantees issued by Strides to Stelis were cut by almost INR600 crores and net debt was heading to about INR450 crores including DSRA deposits, with Stelis guided to turn PAT-positive.
points.quote: We have also reduced our corporate guarantees issued by Strides by almost INR 600 crores and debt -- including new debt that is just being in the process of being secured, will mean that the net debt will come down quite significantly to about INR 450 crores, including DSRA deposits that we have.

points.point: Lenders were an explicit party to the separation — all significant lender NOCs were secured, and lenders accepted release of Strides' guarantees because the new company would carry correspondingly less debt.
points.quote: We have received all the significant NOCs from lenders, which has now been secured, and we look positively forward to a great outcome from OneSource.

points.point: A funding motive: OneSource could raise up to $100 million at relisting, with the new facility taken only as a bridge to the listing, after which Strides' guarantees go off the balance sheet within 12 months.

points.point: Asked whether Strides was giving up value, Arun Kumar framed Strides shareholders as the principal beneficiaries of OneSource, compensating them for having sustained the business.
points.quote: Don't forget that the Strides shareholders are the biggest beneficiaries of OneSource.

points.point: Process milestone: SEBI and stock exchange approvals were received, described as the last step before the NCLT court process, which management expected to take 3-4 quarters plus ~60 days to list.
points.quote: So we got last night, the demerger approvals from SEBI, which was the last step , prior to the court process of the demerger, which is called the NCLT process.

points.point: CFO stated the purpose plainly on completion — a very high-margin softgel business was given up specifically to create a specialty CDMO platform and deliver value through OneSource's listing; appointed date April 1, 2024 and all financials restated.
points.quote: As Arun mentioned earlier, we demerged a very high -margin soft gelatin business to help create a unique speci alty CDMO platform.

points.point: The balance-sheet outcome: INR283 crores of debt transferred to OneSource, INR464 crores of further debt reduction in 9M FY25, net debt INR1,571 crores, net debt/EBITDA at 2x a quarter early, ROCE up to 14.7% from 12.8%, and a INR3,188 crores demerger gain in discontinued operations.
points.quote: As an update on the guarantees further to the release, all the guarantees that were given to OneSource from Stri des are now fully released, and we do not have any outstanding guarantees as of date.

points.quote: All the INR705 crores of guarantees that were issued have been closed during this year.

points.point: Strides deliberately retains its INR305 crores stake in OneSource rather than selling it to prepay debt, rejecting an investor's suggestion.
points.quote: We don't need to reduce debt, and we think our investment in OneSource is a great strategic outcome.

points.point: Management's own scorecard for the separation is quantified as shareholder distribution via the demerger and listing.
points.quote: And the recent one being we distributed INR 78.8 billion back to shareholders in the form of demerger and listing.

points.point: The softgel demerger is cited as the reason the standing $400 million US aspiration was held rather than raised, and is now guided at $375-$400 million for FY28.
points.quote: This $400 million is there for the last 2 to 3 years, right? And post that, we had a demerger of our soft -gel business.

verdict.rationale: The business being separated is the hospitality business of Prestige Estates Projects Ltd., housed in subsidiary Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited (PHVL), out of the listed real-estate development parent. Management's stated reason is capital, not distress: Irfan Razack said hospitality is where "a lot of capex will be required," that the currently trading hotel assets are already "booming" and throwing "positive numbers from all the assets," and that there is "a huge pipeline of new assets which are either under planning or under construction or approval" that "will definitely require fresh spending" — "hence an IPO will be the need of the day." The demerger-plus-IPO is therefore framed as giving "additional bandwidth to grow the hospitality business," i.e. a dedicated capital pool for a capex-hungry annuity business instead of funding it from the developer's balance sheet. The only parent-side numbers given are balance-sheet ones: management guided that by end-FY2025 cash flows would be "pretty robust" and debt would fall — clarified as debt-to-equity, not absolute debt — helped by land already paid for at Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel turning into positive cash flows. The push came from the sell side and retail holders asking for updates and for a shareholder quota in the IPO (Kunal Lakhan, Rajeev Venkatesh); no lender or JV-partner demand was cited. A related theme is staying within core competence — on data centres, Zayd Noaman said operations are "completely different, and it's not our expertise," preferring build-to-suit (NTT) and partnerships. The structure ultimately executed was a subsidiary IPO: PHVL filed a DRHP on April 24, 2025, then withdrew it on September 25, 2026 "on account of strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions," with a fresh DRHP possible later.
verdict.evolution: On the May 2024 call the hospitality demerger was already "a work in progress" and management committed to the direction — demerger then IPO — on capex and growth-bandwidth grounds. By the October 2024 call it had moved only to the structuring stage: "too early," with Board approval and the appointment of bankers still ahead, and the retail-quota question deferred. The filings then show execution and reversal: a PHVL DRHP dated April 24, 2025, withdrawn on September 25, 2026 for strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions, with a possible refiling subject to market conditions and approvals.

points.point: Asked for an update on the hospitality demerger, Irfan Razack confirmed it was under way and endorsed the direction as the right one.
points.quote: That's a work in progress and I believe that that's the way to go.

points.point: The core driver given is the capital intensity of hospitality — the demerger plus IPO is meant to create headroom to grow it, since trading assets are performing and a large pipeline is in planning, construction or approval.
points.quote: And once we do the demerger and we do an IPO that will give us additional bandwidth to grow the hospitality business because currently the hospitality business is booming and we're getting positive numbers from all the assets, current assets which are trading and we do have a huge pipeline of new assets which are either under planning or under construction or approval.

points.point: The new pipeline needs fresh money, which management said makes the IPO necessary rather than optional.
points.quote: So all this will definitely require fresh spending and hence an IPO will be the need of the day.

points.point: Parent-side context: land already funded at Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel turns into cash inflows, supporting deleveraging through FY2025 — clarified as debt-to-equity, not absolute debt.
points.quote: So we believ e that the debt levels for the end of financial year 2025 of course there'll be blips up and down quarter -on-quarter, but the cash flows will be pretty robust, and we will try and bring down the debt level from what it is today.

points.point: Five months later the transaction was still only being structured, with Board approval and banker appointments yet to come — so no terms, ratio or timeline were available.
points.quote: It is too early right now. We are in the structuring process.

points.point: A retail shareholder asked for a reserved shareholder quota in the hospitality IPO; management deferred the decision to a later stage.
points.quote: So maybe how much will be the retail quota for the existing shareholders, we'll figure at that point of time once we -- more advanced.

points.point: On data centres, management drew a competence boundary — it will sell land and build to suit (NTT) but not operate — consistent with housing operating-intensive businesses separately or with partners.
points.quote: So with that, we'll build some expertise, but the operations of a data center are completely different, and it's not our expertise.

points.point: The separation was executed as a subsidiary IPO: Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited filed a DRHP dated April 24, 2025 with SEBI, NSE and BSE.
points.quote: We wish to inform you that our subsidiary, Prestige Hospitality Ventures Limited ( “PHVL ”), filed a Draft Red Herring Prospectus dated April 24, 2025 (“DRHP ”) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (“SEBI ”), the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited (“Stock Exchanges ”).

points.point: On September 25, 2026 the PHVL board withdrew the DRHP, citing strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions — no further rationale was disclosed.
points.quote: However, the board of directors of PHVL has decided to withdraw the DRHP on account of strategic considerations and uncertain market conditions, pursuant to its resolution dated September 25, 2026 and corresponding communication dated September 25 , 2026 made to the book running lead managers to the Offer .

points.point: The listing is deferred, not abandoned: PHVL may refile a DRHP later, conditional on markets, approvals and other considerations.
points.quote: Additionally, PHVL may consider filing a fresh draft red herring prospectus with SEBI in the future for an initial public offering of its equity shares in accordance with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018, subject to suitable market conditions, receipt of requisite approvals and other considerations.

verdict.what_management_expects: Hospitality: demerger plus IPO gives bandwidth and fresh equity for heavy capex on its pipeline under planning, construction and approval, while trading assets already give positive numbers. Parent: cash flows from Indirapuram, Prestige City Hyderabad and Budvel land bring debt-to-equity down by FY2025. No margin or valuation targets stated.
verdict.gaps: No hospitality revenue, EBITDA, keys or capex numbers; no debt quantum, scheme rationale text, entitlement ratio, asset-debt split, lender or partner consent, valuation, timeline, or what "strategic considerations" meant.

verdict.rationale: The texts supplied do not contain any statement of why SKF India is separating the business — neither call passage nor filing gives a rationale, a strategic motive, or a requesting party. What they do establish is the mechanical fact pattern: SKF India Limited (the Demerged Company) demerged its industrial undertaking into SKF India (Industrial) Limited (the Resulting Company), incorporated 17 December 2024, under a Scheme of Arrangement between the two companies and their respective shareholders and creditors, sanctioned by the NCLT on 26 September 2025, with the Resulting Company's shares listed on the Main Board of BSE and NSE from 5 December 2025 and its CIN changed from U28140PN2024PLC236396 to L28140PN2024PLC236396. The separation created a standalone industrial entity whose history is not comparable: management reports quarter-on-quarter because year-on-year figures required extraction from SKF India Limited's books for 17 Dec 2024–31 Mar 2025 and 1 Apr 2025–30 Sep 2025 under Appendix C of Ind AS 103, with management assumptions. The only costs attributed to the separation are one-time: roughly INR 1.8 billion in Q3 FY26 (demerger IT costs, professional services and a large stamp duty on the land transfer from SKF India to SKF India (Industrial) Limited) and INR 183 million in Q4 FY26, mainly demerger-related IT. Q4 FY26 (Jan–Mar) sales were INR 9.5 billion, up 9.8% QoQ, with PBT of 9.5% — a 1,731 bps QoQ improvement — or 11.5% excluding one-offs versus 13.1% in Q3 on the same basis; net working capital fell 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales. The standalone entity's FY mix was roughly 35% distribution, 51% OEM, 6% exports, 4% sales to SKF India and 3% other income, with OEM up 31% YoY (general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy 7%, railway 11%, metals 6%) — and management framed OEM as lower-margin business that builds long-term aftermarket. No problem to be solved, no investor, lender or partner request, and no valuation or capital-structure argument appears anywhere in these texts.
verdict.evolution: No evolution can be reconstructed: only one call is supplied (13 May 2026), which discusses the demerger purely as a completed event affecting comparability, one-time costs and margin optics. The document labelled 'scheme rationale' is in fact a 9 February 2026 stock-exchange intimation about the CIN change and listed status, which records the NCLT sanction (26 September 2025) and the 5 December 2025 listing but contains no rationale section. The earlier calls that would show how the idea surfaced and changed are absent from the material provided.

points.point: Records the Scheme of Arrangement between SKF India Limited (Demerged Company) and SKF India (Industrial) Limited (Resulting Company) and their shareholders and creditors, sanctioned by NCLT on 26 September 2025. points.point: The Resulting Company's equity shares were listed on BSE and NSE Main Board effective 5 December 2025 (NSE: SKFINDUS, BSE: 544572), and its CIN and MCA status changed from unlisted to listed.
points.quote: In compliance with the NCLT Order, the equity shares of the Company were listed on the Main Board of BSE Limited (“BSE”) and National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“NSE”) with effect from December 05, 2025.

points.point: Pre-demerger financials for 17 Dec 2024–31 Mar 2025 and 1 Apr 2025–30 Sep 2025 were extracted from SKF India Limited's records for the demerged industrial undertaking under Appendix C of Ind AS 103, involving management assumptions.
points.quote: Please note that financial information from 17th December 2024 to 31st March 2025 and from 1st April 2025 to 30th September 2025 as reported in the presentation shared has been extracted and may involve some assumptions by the management from the financial information of SKF India Limited pertaining to the demerged industrial undertaking.

points.point: Because of that extraction, management reports quarter-on-quarter rather than year-on-year, comparing Jan–Mar 2026 with Oct–Dec 2025.
points.quote: So, we are reporting quarter -on-quarter , which is we are comparing here Q3 of the financial year to Q4 of the financial year.

points.point: Q4 FY26 standalone performance: INR 9.5 billion of sales, up 9.8% QoQ, with PBT at 9.5% — a 1,731 bps QoQ improvement — and net working capital down 2.8% QoQ to 18.7% of sales.
points.quote: We had a sales growth of 9.8% with INR 9.5 billion of sales.

points.point: Stripping demerger one-offs, Q4 PBT was 11.5% versus 13.1% in Q3 FY26 — i.e. the headline swing from negative 7.8% to positive 9.5% is largely a one-off artefact of the separation.
points.quote: If we remove that, remove the impact of that, this quarter we delivered a margin of 11.5% -- or profit before tax of 11.5%.

points.point: Q3 FY26 one-time demerger charges of about INR 1.8 billion comprised demerger IT costs, professional services and a large stamp duty on the land transfer from SKF India to SKF India (Industrial) Limited.
points.quote: The one -time charges which happened in the previous quarter and in this quarter included, in the previous quarter, it included some IT -related costs related to the demerger, professional services, and a large stamp duty which was paid related to the land transfer from SKF India to SKF India (Industrial ) Limited.

points.point: Q4 FY26 carried a further INR 183 million of demerger-related costs, primarily IT.
points.quote: In this quarter, we again had demerger -related IT costs, primarily that, totalling up to INR 183 million.

points.point: The underlying 13.1% to 11.5% margin decline was attributed to mix, not to the separation: fast-growing lower-margin OEM against higher-margin distribution, with OEM up 31% YoY.
points.quote: Our OEM business grew significantly and as a result, the mix of lower margin OEM business compared to higher margin distribution business accounted for most of this drop.

points.point: Full-year mix of the separated entity: distribution ~35%, OEM ~51%, exports ~6%, sales to SKF India ~4%, other income ~3%; within OEM, railway 11%, general machinery 7%, wind and defence 7%, heavy 7%, metals 6%.
points.quote: full financial year, our distribution was at around 35% and OEM business was around 51%.

points.point: A residual related-party link remains post-separation: about 4% of full-year revenue is sale to SKF India.
points.quote: Exports were at around 6 % and sale to SKF India was at around 4 % and other income was around 3 %.

points.point: Guidance ties margin normalisation to demerger costs rolling off by end of calendar 2026 plus a mix shift back toward distribution, targeting a little above 13%.
points.quote: So given the recent demerger expenses, right, by we would say towards the end of this calendar year, we see that mostly normalizing. We should get back to a little more around 13%.

verdict.what_management_expects: For the separated industrial entity only: demerger costs (INR 1.8bn in Q3, INR 183mn in Q4) mostly ending by end of calendar 2026, PBT margin recovering from 11.5% to a little above 13% as distribution mix normalises against lower-margin OEM, continued working-capital discipline at 18.7% of sales, and OEM wins feeding higher-margin aftermarket. Nothing stated about the retained SKF India entity, capital allocation or valuation.
verdict.gaps: Everything about motive: why separate, who asked, strategic or governance logic, capital and valuation case, what the retained SKF India entity keeps. Earlier calls and the actual rationale text absent.

verdict.rationale: Per the scheme's own rationale, HEG Advanced Materials Ltd. (the First Petitioner / Demerged Company, CIN L23109MP1972PLC008290, incorporated 27 October 1972, registered office at Mandideep near Bhopal, Dist. Raisen, M.P.) says its two core businesses — manufacturing graphite electrodes (including other carbon products) and generation of thermal and hydel power — have each 'acquired critical mass' and now each need flexibility and independence to grow faster in a fast-changing, technology- and innovation-driven environment. The filing argues the two have differentiated strategies, different industry-specific risks, different market dynamics and different growth trajectories, and that the nature of competition in each is distinct, so each is capable of attracting a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders; a structure 'amenable for future growth' is therefore required. verdict.rationale: Management says IGL is being split because its three businesses — the chemicals/green-chemistry business (retained in India Glycols), the Liquor plus Bio-Fuel business (going to IGL Spirits), and the herbal/biopharma business plus the small Bio Polymers (guar gum) business carved out of chemicals (going to Ennature Bio Pharma) — have, in Rupark Sarswat's words, "slightly different priorities, different markets, different drivers," and so should be run and grown independently. The board approved the scheme on 4 February 2025 along with the merger of promoter holding company Kashipur Holdings Limited into IGL, which is intended so that "the promoters will have the direct shareholding of IGL in their names." Anand Singhal sized the three entities on 9MFY25 numbers: India Glycols (chemicals) Rs. 1,079 crores turnover at 13.6% EBITDA margin; IGL Spirits (liquor + biofuel) Rs. 1,628 crores net turnover at 14.4%; Ennature Bio Pharma (biopharma + biopolymer) Rs. 178 crores at 14.9%. The stated benefits are four: independent growth for each business, reduced risk of one business affecting the others, potential value unlock "by drawing focused investors," and clear focus leading to improved management and resource allocation. Mechanically it is an NCLT-route demerger effective 1 April 2026 with all three companies to be listed, requiring SEBI, lender and NCLT approvals over a 12–15 month timeline, and the consortium lead State Bank of India is being engaged on splitting working capital and term debt. The debt split was progressively disclosed: Rs. 1,200 crores long-term debt in May 2025 (Rs. 500 crores chemicals / Rs. 700 crores liquor), then Rs. 1,400 crores in November 2025 split Rs. 600 crores India Glycols / Rs. 800 crores IGL Spirits, against which a Rs. 467 crores raise plus Rs. 180 crores of scheduled repayment was being applied. The demerger has also become the gating item for capital allocation and credit: capex is deferred until after it, and the credit rating sits on watch list with no upgrade possible until completion. Spirits was shown as the higher-return leg (ROCE of 17–18% per May 2025), while an investor challenged the logic of demerging Ennature given its margin collapse, which management conceded as a "margin squeeze" rather than degrowth.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced fully formed on the Feb 2025 call, where Sarswat opened with "the initiation of the scheme, which proposes to restructure IGL into three de-merged identities" following the 4 February 2025 board approval, with Singhal giving segment P&Ls, the Kashipur Holdings merger, the 1 April 2026 effective date and a 12–15 month approval runway. Through May 2025, Aug 2025 and Nov 2025 the discussion shifted from rationale to plumbing — allocating long-term debt between the entities (Rs. 500/700 crores, later Rs. 600/800 crores), deferring all large capex until after the split, and defending Ennature's economics against an investor who called its margins trading-like. By Feb 2026 the demerger had become a constraint as well as a plan: the credit rating was frozen on watch list until completion and capex explicitly postponed, and by the Jun 2026 call (transcript dated 18 May 2026) attention was on the NCLT second-motion hearing of 21 May 2026 and hopes of an order in the first ten days of June, after which ROC filing would follow.

verdict.rationale: On the texts supplied, the separation is not JSW Energy carving out one of its own businesses: it is GE Power India Limited (GEPIL) demerging its boiler manufacturing business into JSW Energy Limited (JSWEL), with GEPIL as Transferor/Demerged Company and JSWEL as Transferee/Resulting Company under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act 2013. The only rationale management actually gives is on the October 2025 call, and it is an acquisition/vertical-integration rationale rather than a separation-of-conglomerate rationale: "This acquisition significantly enhances our in -house capabilities wit h both technology and people which is very critical for equipment manufacturing and supports our thermal power expansion plan." It sits inside a stated growth ambition of "capacity of 30 GW and 40 GWh of energy storage," pursued "in a calibrated and strategic manner" to "ensure predictability in execution." It is explicitly one of a bundle of three same-quarter moves: the GEPIL boiler scheme, completion of a majority stake in KSK Water Infrastructure (which supplies raw water to the 1,800 MW KSK Mahanadi plant and is equipped for a further 1,800 MW), and a battery assembly plant in Pune. Management frames it alongside the SANY wind-turbine manufacturing partnership and the decision to pause its own solar module manufacturing plans — i.e. buying in equipment capability where a partner or an acquisition is available, and dropping in-house build where it is not. The scheme filing text provided contains no rationale section at all: it is BSE/NSE observation-letter language that merely *requires* the company to disclose "Need for the demerger, Rationale of the scheme and swap ratio, Synergies of business of the entities involved in the scheme." Consideration appears to be JSWEL shares to GEPIL shareholders, since the exchanges require a table of GEPIL shareholders, the share exchange ratio, and their "Classification in JSWEL post scheme."
verdict.evolution: Only one call passage was supplied, so no multi-call evolution is observable: on the Oct 2025 call the boiler-business scheme is announced as already signed, listed first of three strategic developments for the quarter, with no prior-call build-up in the provided text. The filing trail then runs NSE's reference letter to SEBI dated December 31, 2025, SEBI's comments dated March 30, 2026, and the NSE observation letter dated April 01, 2026, which gives JSW Energy six months to file the scheme with the NCLT. Nothing in the supplied texts shows the plan's terms changing between those dates; SEBI explicitly bars changes to the draft scheme after filing except those mandated by regulators.

verdict.rationale: The trigger was external to India: after parent Unilever PLC announced its intention to separate its ice cream business globally, HUL's Board ran a comprehensive review through an independent committee and decided to separate its own Ice Cream Business Undertaking. The stated business reason is structural mismatch — the scheme cites ice cream's "different operating model," including differentiated infrastructure for supply and distribution (cold chain), distinct capital allocation needs, and a distinct channel landscape and go-to-market strategy, which do not fit the rest of HUL's FMCG machine. Two routes were weighed on the Oct 2024 call — outright sale, or demerge and list — with the decision criteria explicitly stated as maximising shareholder value while minimising business disruption; HUL chose the demerger into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited (KWIL) on a 1:1 share entitlement ratio (Deloitte India Valuation LLP as registered valuer, Kotak Mahindra Capital fairness opinion), so every HUL shareholder directly owns the new listed ice cream company and can stay invested in its growth. Management sized the business as roughly 3% of HUL's turnover earning low single-digit EBITDA margins versus HUL's ~23%, so the carve-out mechanically lifts HUL's reported EBITDA margin by 50-60 bps (guidance 22-23% becomes an implied 22.5-23.5%), while Ritesh Tiwari argued the loss of 3% of turnover does not change HUL's scale at a kirana store. For the ice cream entity, the case is a focused, experienced, dedicated management team with flexibility to run a distinctive operating model, iconic brands (Kwality Wall's, Cornetto, Magnum) in an attractive high-growth category, and continued access to the portfolio, brand, innovation and technical expertise of the largest global ice cream business. For HUL, it is one of a sequence of portfolio-sharpening moves — divestment of atta and salt, divestment of the water business (Pureit, completed 1 Nov, unlocking circa Rs. 600 crores), and redeployment into high-growth demand spaces via Minimalist (turnover over Rs. 500 crores in FY25) and OZiva (Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 400 crores run rate; remaining 49% bought for Rs. 824 crores) — framed as 'fewer, bigger bets'. The scheme also claims a smoother transition for ice cream's people, and ring-fences ice cream creditors' claims onto the Resulting Company (with NCLT directing HUL to ensure KWIL can meet those obligations). Notably, no investor, lender, partner or regulator is named anywhere as having demanded the separation — the parent's global decision plus the Board's own review are the only sources given.
verdict.evolution: Oct 2024: following Unilever's global announcement, HUL confirms separation in principle but not the mode — an independent committee is weighing sale versus demerger-and-listing, with a route decision targeted by end of the calendar year, and ice cream sized at ~3% of business. Jan 2025: the Board approves the scheme of arrangement to demerge into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited at 1:1, with the detailed business rationale having been laid out at the Capital Markets Day, alongside the Pureit divestment and Minimalist acquisition. Apr 2025 and Oct 2025: execution-only updates — on track with regulatory requirements, completion by end-FY2026, then a specified two-step sequence (demerger in the December quarter with ice cream reported as discontinued, listing in Q4 FY26) plus the first explicit margin arithmetic of 50-60 bps. Feb 2026: demerger completed in the December quarter, with one-time non-cash demerger gain inside reported PAT of Rs. 6,603 crores (+121%), continuing-business EBITDA margin of 23.3%, KWIL listing on 16 February; by May 2026 it is cited retrospectively as a completed portfolio-rotation action already improving the growth mix.

points.point: The mode of separation was still open: sale versus demerge-and-list, with an independent committee and then the Board to decide, judged on shareholder value maximisation and minimal business disruption, with a conclusion targeted by end of the year.
points.quote: And of course, the key objective that the independent committee and hence, Board going forward, will end up making a decision on is -what's the best route in which we can maximize shareholder value and minimize business disruption.

points.point: Ritesh Tiwari pre-empted the dis-synergy worry on distribution: ice cream is only ~3% of the business, so HUL's scale at a typical kirana store is not materially changed, and normal growth accretion more than replaces it.
points.quote: So, for typical kirana store, it does not change anywhere materially - the scale at which we operate in the kirana store, it does not impact to start with.

points.point: The process was explicitly framed as a consequence of the parent's decision, with HUL giving sequential quarterly updates on where it stood.
points.quote: And the way we have done -- last quarter we communicated where we were in the process after Unilever globally announced its decision to separate.

points.point: Board approved the scheme to demerge into Kwality Wall's (India) Limited at a 1:1 entitlement, so the entire shareholding sits directly with HUL shareholders and they participate in the new company's value creation.
points.quote: Pursuant to the scheme, 1 equity share of the new entity will be allotted for every 1 equity share held in HUL.

points.point: The stated benefit for the ice cream entity was management focus and strategic flexibility suited to a business model different from HUL's, in a high-growth category with iconic brands.
points.quote: The demerger will equip an experienced management with greater focus and flexibility to deploy strategies suited to its distinctive business

points.point: The demerger was positioned as part of a run of portfolio choices — after the atta and salt divestment, the water (Pureit) divestment, and alongside the Minimalist acquisition — all aimed at sharper focus and higher-growth demand spaces.
points.quote: After the divestment of our atta and salt business, we have continued to drive sharper focus in the business this year by making strategic portfolio choices, including divestment of water business and decision to demerge Ice Cream business.

points.point: Context for the decision: ice cream revenue was flat year-on-year while HUL held EBITDA at 23.7%, PAT BEI flat at INR7,723 crores and PAT up 6% to INR8,151 crores, with near-term EBITDA guided to the lower end of 23-24%.
points.quote: Ice Cream revenue remained flat year -on-year.

points.point: Execution update placing the demerger among value-unlocking portfolio actions (Pureit circa Rs. 600 crores, Minimalist over Rs. 500 crores turnover, OZiva Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 400 crores), with completion guided to end-FY2026.
points.quote: The demerger of Ice cream business Is progressing on track with regulatory requirements, and we expect It to be completed by the end of financial year 2026.

points.point: First explicit margin quantification: ice cream runs below HUL's average margin, so its removal adds 50-60 bps to reported EBITDA margin on top of the unchanged 22-23% guidance (which management stressed was not an upgrade).
points.quote: Coming to EBITDA margin, Ice Cream demerger is expected to result in an improvement of 50-60 bps to the reported margin as Ice Cream business operates at a margin lower than HUL average.

points.point: Size and profitability of the carved-out business restated — roughly 3% of turnover at low single-digit margin, running even below that this year because of monsoon impact and investments.
points.quote: Ice Cream, as we had called out even earlier, it's roughly 3-odd percentage of our business. and the business makes low single-digit margin.

points.point: Mechanics spelled out as two steps: demerger in the December quarter with ice cream reported as discontinued business, then listing in the March quarter, subject to regulatory approvals.
points.quote: Second, in March quarter at the end of the financial year, we'll end up listing the company.

points.point: The separated business was deteriorating at the point of exit, hit by an extended monsoon on top of the GST transition.
points.quote: Ice Cream business declined year on year, impacted by extended monsoon in addition to GST transition.

points.point: Demerger completed in the December quarter; reported numbers now exclude ice cream, with continuing-business EBITDA of Rs. 3,788 crores (23.3% margin) and reported PAT of Rs. 6,603 crores up 121%, inflated by a one-time non-cash demerger gain and OZiva/Minimalist fair valuation.
points.quote: And the second item is one- time non -cash gain arising from Ice Cream demerger accounted for in accordance with the approved scheme of demerger and applicable accounting standards.

points.point: The forward case for the standalone entity rests on dedicated management and singular focus capturing India's growing ice cream opportunity; listing date set for 16 February.
points.quote: With a dedicated management team and singular focus, we are confident that KWIL is well positioned to capitalise on the growing market opportunity in India and deliver sustained performance.

points.point: Niranjan Gupta confirmed the post-demerger margin framing: the 22-23% guidance stands with the ~50 bps ice cream benefit on top, i.e. an implied 22.5-23.5%.
points.quote: We also outlined that the range, therefore, you will see a benefit of the ice cream demerger to the extent of 50 basis points.

points.point: Retrospective framing: the demerger plus OZiva and Minimalist are described as portfolio rotation that is already improving the quality and growth profile of the remaining business, alongside Rs. 2,000 crores of premium Beauty and Home Care capex and a Unified India reorganisation.
points.quote: Strategic actions such as the demerger of Ice Cream, along with the investments at OZiva and Minimalist, are already enhancing the growth mix of the portfolio.

points.point: The filing names the parent's global announcement as the trigger and lists the structural reasons: a different operating model with differentiated supply and distribution infrastructure, separate capital allocation needs, and a distinct channel landscape and go-to-market strategy.
points.quote: Following the announcement by the Demerged Company’s parent entity, Unilever PLC, of its intention to separate its ice cream business globally, the Board of the Demerged Company had undertaken a comprehensive review and had decided to separate the Ice Cream Business Undertaking in view of its different operating model, including differentiated infrastructure for supply and distribution, capital allocation needs, distinct channel landscape and go-to- market strategy.

points.point: Objective is an independent listed ice cream company — a leading listed player in India built on Kwality Wall's, Cornetto and Magnum, with focused management and flexibility for its distinctive operating model and market dynamics.
points.quote: the Ice Cream Business Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme) operates in an attractive high-growth category and has built iconic brands such as ‘Kwality Wall’s’, ‘Cornetto’ and ‘Magnum’ and the Demerger would create a leading listed ice cream company in India, which will have a focused management with greater flexibility to deploy strategies suited to its distinctive operating model and market dynamics, to realise its full potential;

points.point: The new entity is to retain access to the global ice cream organisation's portfolio, brands, innovation and technical expertise — the implicit answer to why a standalone Indian entity is not disadvantaged.
points.quote: the Resulting Company will have ability to benefit from the portfolio, brand and innovation resources and technical expertise from the largest global ice cream business enabling it to keep winning in the market space;

points.point: Benefits claimed for the remaining HUL are sharper focus and acceleration in high-growth demand spaces to strengthen a future-fit portfolio, plus value unlock and optionality for shareholders to stay invested in ice cream, and a smoother transition for ice cream's people.
points.quote: the Demerger will enable the Demerged Company to drive sharper focus in the business as it further accelerates its play in high- growth demand spaces, strengthening its future fit portfolio;

points.point: Consideration is a straight 1:1 share entitlement, valued by Deloitte India Valuation LLP with a Kotak Mahindra Capital fairness opinion; ice cream creditors' claims pass entirely to the Resulting Company, with NCLT directing HUL to ensure KWIL can meet those obligations.
points.quote: for every 1 (one) equity share of face value of Re. 1/- fully paid up held in the Demerged Company, 1 (one) equity share(s) of face value of Re. 1/- credited as fully paid up in the Resulting Company

verdict.what_management_expects: For HUL: ~50-60 bps higher reported EBITDA margin (22-23% guidance becoming an implied 22.5-23.5%), sharper focus and capital redeployed into high-growth spaces (Beauty & Wellbeing, Foods, OZiva, Minimalist), with an improved growth mix and no material loss of kirana-level scale. For KWIL: a leading listed Indian ice cream company with dedicated management, flexibility for its own cold-chain and channel model, continued global brand/innovation/technical support, and value unlock via direct 1:1 shareholding.

verdict.rationale: Despite the framing of a "separation," what the texts describe is an inbound restructuring: Gabriel India is not carving out one of its own businesses but receiving one. On 1 July 2025 the Board approved a composite scheme in which Anchemco India Private Limited (formerly Andasia Private Limited) first amalgamates into the promoter holding vehicle Asia Investments Private Limited (AIPL), after which AIPL's "Automotive Undertaking" is demerged into Gabriel India as the Resulting Company — bringing four promoter-held entities and JVs (Anchemco, Dana Anand, Henkel ANAND and ANAND CY Myutec) under the listed company. Management's stated reasons were threefold: convert Gabriel from a single-product company (suspension/ride-control) into a diversified product company; deepen collaboration with foreign strategic partners (Dana, Henkel, CY Myutec; Inalfa was cited separately on technology) and capture economies of scale, shared resources, a wider customer base, supply-chain synergies and a bigger aftermarket portfolio; and simplify the group structure so that Gabriel becomes "the growth engine for the automotive business." Chairperson Anjali Singh tied it to a group revenue ambition of INR50,000 crores by 2030 and positioned Gabriel as the group's vehicle for future growth and long-term value creation. The explicit investor angle was named by management itself: the deal "addresses the repeated queries of investors on product diversification, M&A" by folding mature JVs into Gabriel. The financial argument was that Gabriel scales up with no leverage and no cash outlay, with roughly 40% EPS accretion on a current-scale basis and an enhanced ability to raise funds for future organic and inorganic growth. Costs/risks flagged in the filing rather than the calls: promoter shareholding rises on implementation, with NSE requiring the company to explain that increase and its impact on public shareholders' rights and value; approvals needed were creditors, SEBI/stock exchanges, NCLT and majority-of-minority shareholders over a 10–12 month timeline.
verdict.evolution: The idea surfaced fully formed on the 1 July 2025 transaction call, held a day after Board approval and restricted by the moderator to the announced transaction, where management said it had been "actively evaluating organic and inorganic opportunities" and named the four target entities, the two-step merger-then-demerger mechanics, a 10–12 month approval timeline and ~40% EPS accretion. By the 10 February 2026 call the plan had not changed in substance, only advanced procedurally: NSE no-objection (observation letter dated 17 November 2025), NCLT application filed, first motion heard in early January 2026 and the scheme admitted by order dated 29 January 2026, with management stressing it was "very much on track" against the original timeline; the NCLT-directed shareholder meeting was convened for 18 March 2026. On the 28 May 2026 call, management confirmed shareholder and NCLT approvals and an effective date of 22 May 2026, i.e. roughly the 10–12 months originally guided, alongside an FY26 dividend of INR5 per share versus INR4.7 in FY25. Across the three calls no change in scope, consideration or entity list is disclosed in these passages.

points.point: Chairperson Anjali Singh framed the composite scheme as a corporate-structure realignment to unlock synergies and sharpen competitiveness, with Gabriel as the group's growth vehicle and platform for long-term value creation.
points.quote: This scheme of arrangement marks a meaningful step forward in realizing our group's strategic vision, realigning the corporate structure to unlock synergies and enhance our competitive edge.

points.point: The group-level ambition behind the restructuring was quantified as INR50,000 crores of group revenue by 2030, with Gabriel leading it.
points.quote: With an ambitious group revenue target of INR50,000 crores by 2030, Gabriel India is poised to lead the charge, redefining its legacy and setting new benchm

points.point: Management said it had been evaluating organic and inorganic options and had identified promoter-held businesses and investments to acquire through a scheme rather than a cash purchase.
points.quote: Also, we have identified a few businesses and investments for potential acquisition through a scheme of arrangements, which have been held by the promoters of Gabriel.

points.point: Four target entities were named on the call: Anchemco, Dana Anand, Henkel ANAND and ANAND CY Myutec.
points.quote: S o right now, we are looking at four entities An chemco, Dana Anand, Henkel ANAND and A NAND CY Myutec.

points.point: Mechanics were two-step (Slide 7): Anchemco merges into AIPL first, then the automotive undertaking is demerged out of AIPL into Gabriel.
points.quote: So as a first step, the merger of Anchemco into AIPL happens, then deme

points.point: Approvals required were creditors, NCLT, stock exchanges, shareholders including majority of minority, over a guided 10–12 month timeline.
points.quote: This is obviously subject to the key approvals from the creditors, NCLT, stock exchanges, shareholders, majority of minority and the time lines that we are looking at is 10 to 12 months subject to the regulatory approvals.

points.point: Rationale one: move Gabriel from a single-product company to a diversified product company, with closer work with the foreign strategic partners and scale/shared-resource synergies.
points.quote: We are looking at enhanced collaboration with the foreign strategic partners and obviously, achieving synergies through economies of scale and shared resources.

points.point: Rationale two: domestic dominance plus global presence — a wider customer base, supply-chain synergies, use of global relationships and a larger portfolio that also lifts aftermarket presence.
points.quote: So we look at expanding the customer base, we are looking at better supply chain synergies, leveraging the global relationships and obviously the larger product portfolio, wherein we are also able to enhance our aftermarket presence.

points.point: Rationale three: simplify the group structure by consolidating AIPL's demerged automotive undertaking into Gabriel, making Gabriel the group's automotive growth engine.
points.quote: So this will consolidate the business of demerged undertaking of AIPL into automotive components making Gabriel the growth engine for the automotive business in the future.

points.point: Management explicitly said the deal answers investors' repeated questions about product diversification and M&A by bringing the group's mature JVs inside the listed entity.
points.quote: And this also add resses the repeated queries of investors on product diversification, M&A by br inging the existing mature JVs under Gabriel fold.

points.point: Financially, Gabriel gains scale with no debt and no cash payout, with ~40% EPS accretion on current scale and better capacity to fund future growth.
points.quote: This helps Gabriel scale up without any leverage or cash outlay, accretion of EPS has been already explained by the Chairperson.

points.point: The 40% figure and the fundraising argument were stated on a current-scale basis as part of the same rationale slide.
points.quote: We are looking at a 40% on a current scale basis and the enhanced ability to raise the funds for future organic and inorganic growth.

points.point: Dana Anand, one of the demerged JVs, was described as dating back to 1993 — management's point that these are mature, established businesses rather than start-ups.
points.quote: If you look at Dana Anand was established in 1993.

points.point: Management said it remains open to opportunities outside India and had explored a couple that did not clear its value-for-stakeholders test.
points.quote: A couple of them, to be honest, we have explored.

points.point: Investor Viraj Kacharia (Q&A) pressed for near-term and medium-term synergy quantification, noting existing sales interlinks between Gabriel and the target entities.
points.quote: So I'm just trying to ask is, are there any low -hanging fruits either in terms of synergies you think, be it sales or costs, which can play out in the near term for you?

points.quote: So I can give you a couple of examples, again of the synergies that we see in the, I would say, in the short run.

points.quote: So on the scheme of arrangement, we received the NOC from st ock exchange and post that, we filed our application to NCLT.

points.point: First motion was heard in early January 2026 and the scheme admitted with the order announced by end-January, available on the NCLT website.
points.quote: I'm happy to share that the first motion hearing happened in early January.

points.point: Management insisted the scheme was running to the originally guided timetable, i.e. no change to the plan.
points.quote: So we are very much on track what original time we had planned for this scheme and we've been p rogressing very well on this front.

points.quote: There, definitely, I think Inalfa being very strong in technology, we are also trying to offer some newer technology products to customers.

points.point: The portfolio was framed as a mix of standard and new-technology products with differing margins, the stated aim being to bring in more technology.
points.quote: The idea is to bring more technology.

points.point: Management confirmed completion: Anchemco into AIPL, then demerger of the automotive undertaking into Gabriel, with shareholder and NCLT approvals received.
points.quote: So, I would like to update you all that the composite scheme involving the amalgamation of Anchemco India Private Limited into Asia Investment Private Limited followed by the demerger of automotive undertaking into Gabriel India has now received key shareholder and NCLT approvals.

points.point: Alongside the restructuring, FY26 dividend rose to INR5 per share (INR3.1 final plus INR1.9 interim) from INR4.7 in FY25, and management called the Indian auto outlook positive on policy, infrastructure, localization and consumer demand.

points.point: NSE required Gabriel to disclose the need for the merger and demerger, the rationale, the synergies, shareholder impact and a cost-benefit analysis — meaning the rationale itself sits in the shareholder explanatory statement, not in this letter.

points.point: The NCLT ordered the shareholder meeting on 29 January 2026; it was convened for 18 March 2026 by video conference, with e-voting 15–17 March and an 11 March cut-off.
points.quote: The notice is being circulated pursuant to the directions issued by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai bench vide its order dated January 29, 2026, for the purpose of considering and, if deemed appropriate, approving the proposed Scheme, with or without modification(s), under Sections 230 to 232 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act, 2013.

points.quote: The validity of this “Observation Letter” shall be six months from November 17, 2025 , within which the Scheme shall be submitted to NCLT.

verdict.rationale: Inox Green Energy Services (IGESL) is hiving off its Power Evacuation / substation, connectivity and common-infrastructure business into Inox Renewable Solutions Ltd (IRSL, the renamed Resco Global, which already runs the evacuation and EPC business), so that IGESL becomes a pure-play, zero-capex, annuity wind/solar O&M company and IRSL consolidates all evacuation plus EPC into one entity. The scheme's stated logic is that O&M and power evacuation have separate and distinct risks, rewards, financial profiles, competition and opportunities, and that the evacuation business can attract a different set of investors, strategic partners, lenders and other stakeholders, so consolidating it in IRSL unlocks value and gives each business independent focus; the scheme ends in two listed entities, one O&M and one EPC+evacuation. Management's central operating argument is accounting distortion: roughly INR1,000 crores of gross block sits on IGESL's balance sheet for substations on which it is, in Devansh Jain's words, only a trustee — already paid for by customers — and that block drags about INR50-55 crores of annual depreciation that masks true profitability, so EBITDA has had to be used as a proxy for PAT. Removing it makes the balance sheet 'cleaner and asset light', eliminates the depreciation, raises PBT by that amount (PBT becomes roughly equal to EBITDA and to cash profit, against FY27 EBITDA guidance of upwards of INR600 crores), and significantly improves ROE and ROCE, while only INR4-5 crores (later described as about INR10 crores) of revenue leaves and interest cost is unaffected. The transfer could not be done earlier because moving the historical substations would have required consent from over 200 O&M customers, who management said would have used it to renegotiate contracts and damage the O&M business; all new substations and transmission lines are already being built under Resco, so there is no future evacuation capex in IGESL. Shareholders also get paper: IGESL shareholders receive IRSL shares (management cited broadly 20% of Resco) with automatic listing of IRSL, which had raised INR175 crores at about a INR7,400 crores valuation, and the INR700 odd crores of accumulated tax losses stay with IGESL because they sit at company level, not asset level. The pressure came mainly from analysts and investors who could not isolate O&M EBITDA (Jatin Chawla, Nov 2023) and who repeatedly asked what the demerger does to revenue, depreciation, tax losses and value unlocking; debenture holders representing 100% in value voted unanimously in favour, and shareholders and creditors approved before NCLT sanction.
verdict.evolution: The seed appears in the [Nov 2023] call, where management could not show clean O&M EBITDA because traded-goods margins of INR7-8 crores, IPO charges and the fact that the entity 'had not been demerged from the EPC perspective' were mixed in. By [Aug 2024] the board had appointed consultants and registered valuers for the demerger of the power evacuation business, with a 6-9 month timeline, consequential listing of Resco, and the trustee/200-customer explanation of why it had not happened earlier; [Nov 2024] repeated that status verbatim. In [Feb 2025] the scheme was drafted with BSE/NSE approvals expected in early February and NCLT taking a further 6-9 months, Resco renamed Inox Renewable Solutions, and sizing added (20% of Resco to IGESL holders, INR700 crores tax losses retained); by [Sep 2025] exchange no-objections were in and the scheme filed at NCLT Ahmedabad with the INR1,000 crores gross block / INR50-55 crores depreciation framing, [Nov 2025] added shareholder and creditor approval and recast IRSL as Inox Wind's EPC arm, [Feb 2026] had it in final NCLT hearings, and [Jun 2026] reported NCLT approval with the depreciation already eliminated and IRSL listing pending administrative approvals.

points.point: Analysts could not extract O&M EBITDA because traded-goods margins (INR7-8 crores, under related-party compliance), one-time charges and IPO expenses were mixed in, and because the entity had not been separated from the EPC side — the earliest signal of the structural muddle the demerger later fixes.
points.quote: Plus, there were various other charges given that this entity had not been demerged from the EPC perspective plus the charges for the IPO.

points.point: Management admitted the disclosed segment numbers could not be unpicked by investors and offered a separate call with the finance team on one-time and IPO items.
points.quote: No, you won't be able to find that out because we could not apportion the profit margin on the traded goods in that.

points.point: The board formally appointed consultants and registered valuers to evaluate the demerger of the power evacuation business from Inox Green, with initiation subject to valuation reports and board approval.
points.quote: The board of Inox Green has appointed consultants and registered valuers for evaluating the demerger of power evacuation business from Inox Green.

points.point: The stated benefit was a cleaner, asset-light balance sheet plus value added through elimination of depreciation.
points.quote: Demerger of power infrastructure facilities currently on the balance sheet of Inox Green will result in a cleaner and asset light balance sheet.

points.point: Devansh Jain gave a 6-9 month timeline from board approval and said the outcome would be the consequential listing of Resco carrying Inox Green's power evacuation infrastructure.
points.quote: And post evaluation of reports and subject to the Board approval, the demerger would take place, which would lead to consequential listing of Resco, along with the power evacuation infrastructure of Inox Green.

points.point: The core problem: Inox Green is only a trustee of historical substations already paid for by customers, and they could not be moved to Resco earlier without consent from over 200 O&M customers who would have renegotiated contracts; all new evacuation assets are already built under Resco.

points.point: Management framed residual Inox Green as a zero-capex annuity O&M business with no land banks and no future power evacuation, its balance sheet 'unnecessarily inflated' by the legacy substations.

points.point: Answering investor Bhavya Shah, CFO Manish Garg quantified the P&L impact: no interest-cost effect and only about INR4-5 crores of annual revenue leaving with the demerged assets.
points.quote: So Bhavya, to be very precise, there would be no impact on the interest cost as such, but a little bit of the revenue will go away, which is a very miniscule number.

points.point: Status repeated unchanged a quarter later — valuers and consultants appointed, process to start after valuation reports and board approval, with the same asset-light and depreciation-elimination rationale.
points.quote: The demerger of power infra facilities currently on the balance sheet of INOX Green will result in a cleaner and asset -light balance sheet.

points.point: Akhil Jindal told investors to treat EBITDA as the benchmark for PAT because the heavy depreciation now in Inox Green's numbers will transfer to Resco with the assets — an explicit admission that reported profit understates the business.
points.quote: There is a significant amount of depreciation charges that is being reflected in our current numbers, which would be transferred to Resco as assets get transferred.

points.point: Process detail: BSE/NSE approvals expected in the first week to 15 days of February, then NCLT taking another 6-9 months, with hopes of completion within calendar 2025 and Resco renamed Inox Renewable Solutions Limited being listed.

points.point: Answering investor Deepak Sharma, S.K. Mathusudhana said Inox Green shareholders benefit twice — they receive Resco shares (he cited broadly 10%, then broadly 20% of Resco) and the full depreciation disappears so EBITDA converts to PBT and PAT.

points.point: Asked by analyst Akhilesh whether the demerger removes accumulated tax losses, management confirmed the INR700 odd crores of losses sit at company level, not asset level, and stay with Inox Green.
points.quote: So the tax losses would be on a company level, not on an asset level.

points.point: Scheme received no-objection from the stock exchanges and was filed at NCLT Ahmedabad; management sized the effect as roughly INR1,000 crores of gross block off the balance sheet and INR50-55 crores of annual depreciation eliminated, lifting PBT and improving ROE and ROCE, with approval expected in 2-3 quarters.

points.point: IRSL's standalone value was already being established: INR175 crores raised at roughly INR7,400 crores valuation, with EPC, blade and transformer manufacturing housed there and margin guidance raised to 18-19% for FY26.
points.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

points.point: Investor Hansal Thakkar pushed further, asking whether IGESL and IRSL would eventually be demerged into the hands of Inox Wind shareholders; Akhil Jindal restated that the scheme covers only the substation, connectivity and common infrastructure, with automatic listing of Resco giving Inox Green holders its shares.

points.point: Shareholders and creditors approved the scheme; management framed it as value-accretive for both parents — IRSL listing as Inox Wind's EPC arm, Inox Green losing the depreciation on the demerged asset blocks.

points.point: Scheme in final stages of hearing at NCLT Ahmedabad; management reiterated INR1,000 crores gross block and INR50-55 crores depreciation elimination, expecting NCLT approval in about a month and listing 1 to 1.5 months after, i.e. roughly 2-3 months in all, while refusing to commit to dates.
points.quote: Finally, I would like to inform our investors that the scheme of demerger of substation business from Inox Green and its subsequent merger into Inox Renewable Solutions is in the final stages of hearing at Hon ’ble NCLT Ahmedabad.

points.point: With zero depreciation post demerger and virtually nil finance cost, management confirmed to analyst Utkarsh Somaiya that PBT equals EBITDA and equals cash profit on FY27 EBITDA of upwards of INR600 crores, with a 25% deferred tax book entry (accounting PAT ~INR450 crores) but no cash tax outgo because of the tax shield.
points.quote: So, our PBT would be equivalent to EBITDA.

points.point: Revenue leakage was re-quantified for investor Prit Nagersheth as only about INR10 crores leaving against roughly INR50 crores of depreciation — no material impact on the earnings math.
points.quote: So post the demerger, as we have clarified on the multiple cores, there would be a very limited amount of revenue in the range of INR 10 odd crore will get out of the balance sheet.

points.point: NCLT Ahmedabad sanctioned the scheme; the INR1,000 crores gross block and INR50-55 crores of annual depreciation have been eliminated, ROE and ROCE have improved, and IRSL will be automatically listed once remaining approvals are received (Devansh Jain put completion at 1-2 months of administrative process).
points.quote: With this gross block of approximately INR1,000 crores has been elimin ated from Inox Green's balance sheet.

points.point: Rationale (a) continued: the evacuation business is explicitly said to appeal to a different set of capital providers and strategic partners than the O&M business.

points.point: Rationale (b): IRSL already undertakes the Power Evacuation Business, so the arrangement consolidates the same line of business in one entity, unlocking value and lending enhanced focus.

points.point: Rationale (c): the explicit objective is to make IGESL a pure-play O&M player by hiving off power evacuation.

points.point: Rationale (d): the end state is two listed entities — O&M in one, EPC plus power evacuation in the other — each free to pursue its own strategy with independent focus for higher stakeholder growth.
